Bundles that belong to Addressables need their CRC checks cleared with the separate AddressablesTools patchcrc command before edited bundles are used, as the README describes.
MIT per the license file; bundled libraries keep their own terms, including the PVRTexTool license for PVRTexLib, zlib for Unity crnlib and CC BY 4.0 for Font Awesome.

resources.name: Tenet
resources.description: IDA Pro plugin for exploring execution traces of a binary: it loads an externally recorded trace and lets the analyst step forwards and backwards through time while the disassembly shows the execution flow in both directions. Execution, memory and region breakpoints mark every execution of an instruction or every read and write of an address or range along a trace timeline, register seeking jumps to the instruction that set a register's value, and a timestamp shell seeks to a position or percentage of the trace.
requirements: IDA Pro 7.5 or newer on Windows, macOS or Linux; Tenet is a pure Python 3 plugin with no third-party dependencies, installed by copying the repository's plugins folder into IDA's user plugin directory. Release at review: v0.2.0, published 2021-09-14, whose tag is the reviewed master commit.

Tenet only reads traces in its own text format, which records general-purpose register changes and memory reads and writes; a separate tracer must record them, and the repository's Intel Pin tracer for Windows and Linux user-mode programs and its QEMU tracer are marked experimental.
It loads only x86 and AMD64 traces, and its pure-Python reader gives no guarantee that traces of more than 10 million instructions stay reasonable to navigate.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: findcrypt-yara
resources.description: IDA Pro plugin that scans the loaded database with YARA rules for cryptographic constants and similar signatures, lists the matches in a results window and names each matching address after its rule. Its bundled findcrypt3.rules has 126 rules covering constants and tables of hash, cipher and checksum algorithms such as MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, RIPEMD-160, Whirlpool, DES, Blowfish, RC6, TEA and CRC32, big-number and prime constants, crypto API names and functions of libraries such as OpenSSL, Crypto++, MIRACL and FGint; users can add their own .rules files.
requirements: IDA Pro with IDAPython and the yara-python package; the README warns against installing the yara pip package, which is not compatible. Custom rule files go in .idapro/plugins/findcrypt-yara/ under the home directory on Linux and macOS, or in the Hex-Rays IDA Pro plugin folder under %APPDATA% on Windows.
The repository has no releases; the plugin reports version 0.2 with the default hotkey Ctrl-Alt-F, and the reviewed master commit is dated 2024-11-19.
BSD-3-Clause per LICENSE.

resources.name: deREferencing
resources.description: IDA Pro plugin that adds register and stack views to the debugger in which pointers are dereferenced and colored, similar to the context displays of GDB plugins such as PEDA, GEF and pwndbg. It supports x86, x86-64, ARM, ARM64, MIPS32 and MIPS64; both views open from Debugger > Debugger Windows or with Alt-Shift-D and Alt-Shift-E, and a saved desktop layout reopens them in later debugging sessions.
requirements: IDA Pro 7.1 or later. Install it with hcli plugin install dereferencing, or copy dereferencing.py and the dereferencing folder into IDA's plugin directory (.idapro/plugins under the home directory on Linux and macOS, %AppData%\Hex-Rays\IDA Pro\plugins on Windows). Release at review: v2026.09.03, published 2026-09-03, whose tag is the reviewed master commit.
Options are changed in the plugin's config.py file.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: HexRays Toolbox
resources.description: IDAPython scripts that find code patterns in Hex-Rays decompiler output, independent of the binary's processor architecture, by running user-written lambda queries over the decompiled ctree. Queries run from the hxtb-shell GUI inside IDA, from IDAPython through functions such as find_expr() and find_item(), from interactive command-line helpers or in batch mode over a set of files. The README's use cases include finding vulnerabilities and their variants, locating code patterns from previously reversed executables in newly decompiled code, malware variant analysis and finding patterns across binaries built for different architectures.
requirements: Needs a valid IDA license and a valid Hex-Rays decompiler license for each target architecture. The repository has no releases; the reviewed master commit dates from 2023-06-20.
Example queries for hxtb-shell are in the hxtbshell_queries folder, and the shell also accepts Python expressions copied from the context viewer of the separate HRDevHelper plugin.
CC0-1.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: Virtuailor
resources.description: IDAPython tool that reconstructs C++ virtual tables in IDA Pro for 32- and 64-bit Intel and AArch64 code by observing indirect calls while the program runs under IDA's debugger. Its static part finds indirect calls and hooks the assignment of their targets with conditional breakpoints; when those breakpoints hit, the dynamic part creates vtable structures, renames vtables and virtual functions, adds structure offsets to the call instructions and cross-references from each indirect call to the virtual functions it reached, and for AArch64 firmware tries to fix undefined vtables and their functions.
requirements: IDA Pro 7.0 to 7.5: the master branch targets 7.5, and IDA versions older than 7.4 need the beforeIDA-7.4 branch. Run Main.py through File > Run script, ideally after taking an IDB snapshot as the README recommends, then exercise the program under IDA's debugger; AArch64 targets can be debugged through a remote GDB server. The repository has no releases; the reviewed master commit dates from 2020-06-06.
Only vtables used by virtual calls that are hit at run time are reconstructed, and the README says some breakpoints may be missed.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: xAnalyzer
resources.description: x64dbg plugin that annotates the static code of the debugged x86 or x64 executable with function-call, argument and loop analysis. It adds argument and type information from over 13,000 API definitions for almost 200 DLLs, handles undefined and register-based calls generically and detects loops automatically. Analysis runs on a selection, a function or a whole module from menus or the xanal commands, can run automatically at the entry point like OllyDbg's initial analysis, and users can extend its .api and header definition files.
requirements: Needs x64dbg; copy xAnalyzer.dp32 or xAnalyzer.dp64 and the extracted apis_def folder into the matching x64dbg plugin directory. Release at review: 2.5.12, published 2025-08-13, the same day as the reviewed master commit.

The README lists known limits: the first undefined call with generic arguments in a function is not processed unless a jump precedes it, nested calls work correctly only in some cases, loops are detected only within function boundaries and can be misdetected around unconditional jumps, and extended analysis can take much longer and use large amounts of RAM.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: AssetStudio
resources.description: Tool for exploring, extracting and exporting the assets and asset bundles of Unity versions 3.4 to 2022.1. It converts Texture2D and Sprite images to PNG, TGA, JPEG or BMP and AudioClip to MP3, OGG, WAV, M4A or FSB, with FSB-to-WAV conversion, and exports fonts, meshes as OBJ, text assets, shaders, movie and video clips and MonoBehaviour data as JSON; models export from the scene hierarchy, and Animators export to FBX with their bound AnimationClips. MonoBehaviour export asks for the folder holding the assemblies, such as Managed, or, for IL2CPP builds, the dummy DLLs that Il2CppDumper generates.
requirements: Builds target .NET Framework 4.7.2, .NET Desktop Runtime 5.0 or .NET Desktop Runtime 6.0. Building needs Visual Studio 2022 or newer, and the native FBX exporter needs Autodesk's FBX SDK 2020.2.1. The latest release is v0.16.47 (2022-06-16), and the repository is archived on GitHub.
Loading asset bundles decompresses and reads them in memory, which can use a large amount of memory; the README suggests extracting them to a folder first and reading them from there.

The README states that neither the repository, the tool nor its owner is affiliated with, sponsored or authorized by Unity Technologies. MIT per LICENSE; the bundled texture decoders come from separately licensed open-source projects.

resources.name: Voltron
resources.description: Extensible Python debugger UI toolkit that attaches utility views to LLDB, GDB, VDB and WinDbg/CDB sessions. Each view retrieves data from the debugger host and can run in its own terminal, so users can assemble a custom debugger interface; built-in views cover registers, disassembly, stack, memory, breakpoints and backtrace, and any debugger command can be split off into a view highlighted with a chosen Pygments lexer. The views complement the debugger's command line rather than replace it.
requirements: Runs on macOS, Linux and Windows; WinDbg/CDB support goes through PyKD and is described as fairly new. The install script fully supports only macOS and Debian derivatives, and the debugger's init file (.lldbinit or .gdbinit) loads Voltron's entry.py. Architecture support differs by debugger: x86 and x86_64 with all four, ARM except with WinDbg, ARM64 only with LLDB and PowerPC only with GDB.
The newest release is the v0.1.8 pre-release of 2025-01-30, following v0.1.7 from 2016; the reviewed master commit is from the same day as v0.1.8.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: Remill
resources.description: Static binary translation library that lifts AArch64, SPARC32, SPARC64, x86 and amd64 machine code, including AVX and AVX512, into LLVM bitcode, with AArch32 support underway. It focuses on lifting individual instructions accurately and is meant as a library for other tools such as McSema; its documentation walks through how an instruction is lifted, how instruction semantics are implemented and the overall design.
requirements: Supported on Linux and tested on Ubuntu 22.04; it also works on macOS, and Windows support is experimental. Building uses the superbuild in dependencies/ with CMake 3.21+, Ninja, LLVM and Clang 15+, Intel XED, Google Flags, Log and Test and Python 3, and Linux builds can also run in Docker. Release at review: v6.0.1, published 2026-04-21; the reviewed master commit dates from 2026-08-27.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: iaito
resources.description: Official Qt-based graphical interface for the radare2 reverse-engineering framework, aiming for parity with radare2's commands, features and keybindings so that existing r2 plugins and scripts keep working. Its README lists forensics, binary diffing and binary patching alongside disassembly; iaito was the original name before the project was forked as Cutter.
requirements: Needs radare2 and Qt 5 or Qt 6. CI builds and releases cover Linux, macOS and Windows, Linux and WSL users can install it from Flathub (org.radare.iaito), and on macOS the app may need its signature fixed with xattr and codesign as the README shows. Release at review: 6.2.2, published 2026-09-06; the reviewed master commit dates from 2026-11-05.
GPL-3.0 per COPYING.

resources.name: HexRaysCodeXplorer
resources.description: Hex-Rays decompiler plugin for navigating and reconstructing C++ code in IDA's pseudocode window. It reconstructs C++ object types from a selected pointer variable into IDA's local types, identifies virtual function tables and generates structures for them, lets the analyst click through virtual calls once objects are typed, visualizes a function's ctree as a graph, jumps from a pseudocode line to its disassembly and dumps ctrees and types to files. Its Object Explorer lists vtables with cross-references and RTTI parsing, and a batch mode processes many files without user interaction.
requirements: Written in C/C++ for x86/x64 IDA with the Hex-Rays decompiler on Windows, Linux and macOS; the README says only the latest IDA and decompiler versions are tested. The newest GitHub release is 2.1, the IDA 7 edition, from 2018-03-14; the reviewed master commit dates from 2025-11-25.
The repository has no license file and GitHub detects no license.

resources.name: vgmstream
resources.description: Library and tools that decode streamed, prerecorded video game audio in hundreds of formats and codecs, from common game engine files to single-game codecs, including looped music, subsongs, companion files, custom containers and encryption keys. TXTH text descriptors add support for further formats, including raw audio, and TXTP files set per-file options such as forced looping or merging files. It ships as the vgmstream-cli decoder, which converts supported files to WAV, the vgmstream123 player and plugins for Winamp, foobar2000, XMPlay and Audacious, and an online web player is available at vgmstream.org.
requirements: Numbered releases are on GitHub and nightly builds on vgmstream.org; release at review: r2168, published 2026-10-25, and the reviewed master commit dates from 2026-11-05. Users supply the game audio files; doc/FORMATS.md lists the supported formats.
An ISC-style permissive license in COPYING, with portions under their own copyright notices.

resources.name: payload dumper
resources.description: Python script that extracts the partition images, such as boot.img and system.img, from the payload.bin inside an Android OTA update package. It handles full OTAs directly and incremental OTAs with --diff by applying the update to original images that the user copies from a full OTA or dumps from the device, and it can also run from a Docker image.
requirements: Python 3.6 or later with the protobuf package from requirements.txt; the user supplies the OTA package's payload.bin. The README says the script was tested on Yandex Amber OTAs, both full and incremental, under Linux and may also work on Windows.
The repository has no releases, and the reviewed master commit dates from 2025-04-18.
The repository has no license file and GitHub detects no license.

resources.name: Windows Malware Analysis training, volume 1 (malware_training_vol1)
resources.description: Slides and exercises for a Windows malware analysis training that builds an understanding of common malware techniques through programming, reverse engineering and Windows internals, and shows how analysis tools are used for particular goals. Module 1 covers compilation, the PE format, processes, WoW64, shellcode and PE loaders; module 2 introduces malware missions and tactics, hooking, persistence and banking trojans; module 3 introduces evasion and self-defence and fingerprinting, with obfuscation, anti-hooking, deobfuscation and kernel-mode components planned.
requirements: Aimed at people who already know the basics of programming and reverse engineering and want to enter Windows malware analysis. Slides are in slides/ and exercises in exercises/.
The README marks the material as a work in progress: several topics still lack slides or exercises. The reviewed main commit dates from 2024-07-01.
Published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license, per the README; the repository has no license file.

resources.name: IDA NO MCP
resources.description: IDA Pro exporter that turns an analyzed binary into plain files for AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code instead of serving it over MCP. It writes each decompiled function as a .c file, or as .asm when decompilation fails, under a header listing its name, address, callers and callees, along with the string, import and export tables, 1 MB hexdump chunks of every segment and logs of fallbacks, failures and skipped library functions. It ships as an IDA plugin (Export for AI, Ctrl-Shift-E) for small and medium files and as a Rust command-line binary for large or batch exports, which can skip IDA's auto-analysis.
requirements: The plugin, oldpython/INP.py, goes into IDA's plugins directory (%APPDATA%\Hex-Rays\IDA Pro\plugins on Windows, .idapro/plugins under the home directory on Linux and macOS). The Rust binary needs a local IDA Pro 9.x, whose non-redistributable libida and libidalib libraries it links at run time, plus LLVM/Clang for bindgen; it must be built natively on each platform, with an idalib crate version that matches the IDA release, such as idalib 0.9.0 for IDA 9.3sp1.

The Chinese README says the in-IDA plugin can hang on files of 100 MB or more, which the standalone binary's --skip-analysis option avoids. The repository has no releases, and the reviewed main commit dates from 2026-07-26.
The repository has no license file and GitHub detects no license.

resources.name: ida-mcp-rs
resources.description: Headless MCP server written in Rust that drives IDA Pro through idalib, so agents such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI or Cursor can open and analyze binaries without the IDA GUI. Apple targets are single tool calls, including universal Mach-O slice selection, dSYM/DWARF loading and dyld_shared_cache module loading; a 28-tool lean profile sits beside the full tool set, run_script executes IDAPython and returns JSON, and editing tools such as rename, comments, patches and type application each take exactly one address or exact symbol name. save_idb writes checkpoints, and crashed or wedged IDA workers are replaced automatically.
requirements: Needs a released IDA Pro 9.5 with a valid license on the same host architecture, a Hex-Rays decompiler for the target processor for pseudocode tools and working IDAPython for run_script; IDA's first-launch setup, including license acceptance, must be completed by the user. Server versions follow IDA versions (v9.5.x for IDA 9.5, with Homebrew casks for 9.2 to 9.4), and the IDA 9.5 beta runtime is not compatible with the stable server.

Installs through Homebrew, Scoop, Nix or release archives for macOS, Linux and Windows on ARM64 and x86_64; the binary loads IDA's libida and libidalib at run time from standard install paths or IDADIR and library-path variables. Release at review: v9.5.0, published 2026-11-01 and validated with IDA 9.5.261026 on macOS, Linux and Windows ARM64.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: ida-multi-mcp
resources.description: MCP server that lets an agent analyze several IDA Pro databases at once through one endpoint. Each database with its plugin registers itself when opened and headless idalib sessions can be added, and a router exposes up to 76 tools for triage, decompilation and disassembly, cross-references and call graphs, search, types, renaming, comments and patching, plus analysis-wait gating so agents can wait for IDA's auto-analysis to settle; its IDA tool implementations come from the ida-pro-mcp project. Function-similarity search compares functions within or across binaries using name-independent instruction MinHash, API, string and constant anchors and control-flow shape, with optional local neural recall, and nothing is uploaded.
requirements: Needs Python 3.11 or later and IDA Pro 8.5 or later (9.1 or later recommended); IDA 9.0 SP0 (build 240925) is not supported. The package must be installed for both the terminal's Python and IDA's Python, and headless idalib sessions need IDA Pro, because IDA Home and IDA Free do not ship idalib. The repository has no releases; pyproject.toml declares version 0.1.0, and the reviewed main commit dates from 2026-09-19.

The README lists limits: the router binds to localhost only and speaks only stdio, calls to the same IDA instance still run one at a time, cancellation is not forwarded to IDA, and resources need manual routing. Renames, retypes and comments stay in memory until idb_save is called. The optional neural recall downloads its model on demand.
MIT per the README and pyproject.toml; the repository has no LICENSE file.

resources.name: x64dbg MCP (x64dbgMCP)
resources.description: MCP server that connects LLM clients to the x64dbg and x32dbg debuggers through a native plugin and a Python MCP script. It exposes more than 40 tools built on the x64dbg SDK and was tested with Claude and Cursor; agents can query registers, search byte patterns in a module and drive debugging sessions. The README advises giving the model the executable's full path so it can restart a crashed or hung target through the command-execution tool, and starting from GetModuleBase so that queries use valid addresses.
requirements: Needs x64dbg: copy the .dp64 or .dp32 plugin into x64dbg's plugins folder, then register src/x64dbgmcp.py, which needs pip install mcp requests, as the MCP server in the client configuration. Building the plugins needs CMake and MSVC. Release at review: build1.1 (2026-03-15); the README recommends building from source for the latest features, and the reviewed main commit dates from 2026-06-05.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: IDASQL
resources.description: SQL interface to IDA Pro databases that exposes a binary's analysis as more than 30 live virtual tables for agents and scripts. The tables cover functions, segments, names, imports, cross-references, basic blocks, instructions, strings, types, decompilation and annotations, and part of the database can be edited through them. It runs as a standalone CLI that can open raw binaries through idalib, as a plugin in IDA's command-line dropdown, as an HTTP REST or MCP server, or through a skills plugin for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI and Codex, and it can work across several databases at once.
requirements: Needs IDA Pro with its directory on PATH and the idasql release artifact built for the installed IDA version (ida92, ida93 or ida94); plugin binaries are SDK-version-specific. The HCLI-compatible plugin archive covers Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64 and macOS ARM64, with separate ARM64 archives for IDA 9.3 and 9.4. Building from source needs IDA SDK 9.0 or later. Release at review: v0.0.19, published 2026-10-10.
The MCP server serves SSE on a local port and is compiled in by default (-DIDASQL_WITH_MCP=ON); the agent skills live in the separate idasql-skills repository. Deep-link features need IDA 9.4.

Licensed under the Human-Origin Source License v1.0, a source-available license derived in structure from MPL 2.0 that is not OSI-approved: it allows using, building and redistributing unmodified copies, including commercially, but forbids shipping modified versions outside upstream contributions and using the code as an implementation source without the author's written permission.

resources.name: Luyten
resources.description: Graphical Java decompiler front end for the Procyon decompiler, with its editor view powered by RSyntaxTextArea.
requirements: Prebuilt downloads are on the Releases page; building from source uses Maven 3. The newest release was published on 2019-06-06.
Apache-2.0 per license.txt.

resources.name: GDB dashboard
resources.description: Standalone .gdbinit file written with GDB's Python API that shows a modular status interface each time the debugged program stops, reducing the commands needed to inspect its state. No GDB command is redefined; its features sit under a single dashboard command.
requirements: Needs GDB with Python API support; the single .gdbinit file goes in the home directory, and Pygments is optional for syntax highlighting.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: REHex
resources.description: Cross-platform hex editor for reverse engineering that handles files over 1 TB. It adds inline disassembly, integer and floating-point decoding, byte-range annotations, side-by-side comparison, virtual address mapping and bitmap visualisation, with Binary Templates that annotate data automatically and Lua scripting.
requirements: Runs on Windows, Linux, macOS and BSD. Releases provide standalone Windows and macOS packages and Linux packages; 0.64.0 was published on 2026-04-04.
GPL-2.0 per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: Dobby
resources.description: Lightweight, modular hook framework for Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and Linux on x86, x86-64, ARM and ARM64.
requirements: Compiled from source as described in docs/compile.md, or downloaded as a prebuilt library from the release tagged latest, dated 2024-03-14.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: XLMMacroDeobfuscator
resources.description: Command-line tool and Python library that extracts and decodes obfuscated Excel 4.0 (XLM) macros from xls, xlsm and xlsb files. An internal XLM emulator interprets the macros without fully performing the code, and results can be exported as JSON.
requirements: Installed with pip. Loading xls files through Microsoft Excel requires Windows, pywin32 and the --with-ms-excel switch; otherwise the xlrd2 library reads them. The newest release is v0.2.7 from 2022-09-21.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: PE Tree
resources.description: Python module that shows Portable Executable files in a tree view using pefile and PyQt5, as a standalone application and as a plugin for IDA Pro, Ghidra, Volatility, Rekall and minidump. It reads PE images from files, ZIP archives, Windows memory dumps and analysis databases.
requirements: The standalone application needs Python 3.5+ and runs on Windows, Linux and macOS; each plugin needs its host tool. The repository is archived, with the last release 1.0.29 from 2020-10-05.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: RpcView
resources.description: Open-source Windows tool that explores and decompiles the RPC functionality present on a Microsoft system. New rpcrt4.dll runtime versions are added by extending its version table or by reversing the runtime's internal structures.
requirements: Needs the Microsoft Visual C++ 2019 Redistributable; building takes Visual Studio, CMake and Qt5. The README lists runtime support for Windows XP, 7, 8, 8.1 and 10.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: jd-cli
resources.description: Command-line wrapper around a jd-core fork that decompiles Java class and JAR files to the console, a directory or a ZIP file, with options for line numbers, file-matching patterns and parallel processing. It also ships as a Docker image and as a Java library.
requirements: Versions 1.3.0 and later need Java 17+, older ones Java 8+. The newest release is 1.3.0-beta-1 from 2025-10-30.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: amoco
resources.description: Python package for symbolic analysis of binaries. It combines an instruction-decoding framework for adding architectures, a symbolic algebra module that describes instruction semantics, an abstract memory and execution model, and disassembly techniques from linear sweep and recursive traversal to solver-based path-predicate exploration.
requirements: The README marks version 2.9 as under development: x86 FPU semantics and ARM SIMD, VFP, NEON, TrustZone and Jazelle instruction sets are not implemented, some solver-based disassembly strategies are unmerged, and IDB import and export are missing.
GPL-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: Chisel
resources.description: Collection of LLDB commands for debugging iOS apps. Commands print view and view-controller hierarchies, find views by class-name regex, show or hide views without resuming the process, mask or border views, set symbolic breakpoints on a class's method and watchpoints on instance variables, and can be extended with custom commands.
requirements: Installed with Homebrew or by download, then imported from the .lldbinit file in the home directory. Command support differs between iOS and macOS, as the README's command table marks. The newest tagged release is 2.0.1 from 2020-08-17.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: gdbgui
resources.description: Browser-based frontend to the GNU debugger, gdb.
requirements: Documentation lives on gdbgui.com; release 0.15.3.0 was published on 2025-06-29.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: Android Unpacker
resources.description: Code and slides from the Defcon 22 talk "Android Hacker Protection Level 0". It holds a gdb and adb script for Bangcle and SecShell, a native unpacker for APKProtect, Bangcle, LIAPP and Qihoo Packer, tweaks that hide QEMU and debuggers from APKProtect, and a Corellium-based dynamic unpacking approach with automation.
requirements: The gdb-scripts unpacker requires gdb and adb; the native unpacker does not depend on gdb. The newest tagged release is v1.2 from 2014-09-11.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: Porosity
resources.description: Decompiler that turns Ethereum Virtual Machine bytecode into readable Solidity-syntax contracts, supported on Linux and macOS.
requirements: The README marks the project unmaintained and points to the JEB decompiler for smart contracts as an alternative; the newest release is v20180116.2 from 2018-01-16.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: ReverseAPK
resources.description: Command-line tool that decompiles an APK to Java and Smali, lists the extracted files, and statically checks AndroidManifest.xml and the source for common vulnerabilities and behaviours such as intents, command execution, content providers, crypto references and hardcoded secrets.
requirements: Installed with the bundled install script and run as reverse-apk with an APK name; the README describes version 1.2.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: Xori
resources.description: Automation-ready disassembly and static analysis library for shellcode and PE binaries that outputs disassembly, functions and imports as JSON. It offers a light emulation mode that enumerates all paths and a slower full emulation mode, simulated TEB and PEB structures, and FLIRT-style signatures.
requirements: Covers i386 and x86-64 PE, PE+ and plain shellcode. Built with Rust and Cargo; the README cites rustc 1.27.0, and the browser GUI needs Node.js.
AGPL-3.0 per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: binglide
resources.description: Visual reverse-engineering tool that gives a quick overview of the data types present in a file. It reads no particular format, so it also works when headers are missing or corrupted or the format is unknown.
requirements: Needs Python 3, PyQt4 with OpenGL, pyqtgraph and numpy, with numba for JIT speed-ups. The author points to Veles as a more mature successor.
MIT per LICENSE.txt.

resources.name: ERESI
resources.description: Reverse Engineering Software Interface built around ELFsh, an interactive and scriptable shell for reading and modifying ELF objects, and e2dbg, an embedded ELF debugger. ELFsh analyses sections, edits headers and symbol and relocation tables, disassembles through libasm, draws control-flow graphs and injects code into ELF files.
requirements: README.FIRST describes ELFsh 0.65 and is marked as not updated for ERESI 0.8; e2dbg is described for Linux on IA32. The newest release is 0.83-a3-phoenix from 2018-07-09.
The repository has no top-level license file.

resources.name: pixd
resources.description: Terminal tool that visualises binary data like a hexdump, but draws each octet as a coloured square from a palette.
requirements: Needs a terminal emulator that supports 24-bit colour SGR escape sequences.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: Universal Extractor 2
resources.description: Unofficial, extended continuation of Universal Extractor that unpacks files from standard archives, application installers, disk images and game archives. Version 2 adds batch mode, a scan-only mode that detects a file's type, password lists and silent mode.
requirements: Runs on Windows XP or newer; on XP online features are disabled and some extractors may not work. The README links v2.0.0-rc.3.
GPL-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: ElleKit
resources.description: Function hooking toolkit for arm64 XNU devices: a C function hooker that patches memory pages directly, an Objective-C function hooker, an arm64 assembler, JIT inline assembly for Swift and a reimplementation of the Substrate and libhooker APIs. The README lists the Dopamine, palera1n and meowbrek2 jailbreaks as users.
requirements: Needs an arm64 device running the XNU kernel. Tested on iOS 15-27 (arm64), iOS 15-17 (arm64e) and macOS Ventura; the README says it is unsupported on the latest macOS because of code-signing changes.
BSD-3-Clause per LICENSE.

resources.name: xHook
resources.description: PLT hook library for Android native ELF executables and shared libraries. It handles ELF HASH and GNU HASH symbols and SLEB128-encoded relocations, selects targets with regular expressions, and needs no root or system permissions.
requirements: Supports Android 4.0 to 10 on armeabi, armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86 and x86_64; building takes Android NDK r16b.
MIT for the code per LICENSE, with documentation under a Creative Commons license per LICENSE-docs.

resources.name: Epic
resources.description: Continuation of Dexposed on ART: a runtime method-hooking framework that loads into an app and can hook both the app's own code and Android framework code running in its process. Stated uses include instrumentation and security audits.
requirements: The README states support for ART thumb2 and arm64 on Android 5.0 to 11 and none for arm32, x86, x86_64 or MIPS, which rules out Android emulators on those architectures. Short methods and fully inlined methods cannot be hooked. The newest release is 0.11.2 from 2021-07-31.
Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: ProcDump for Linux and macOS
resources.description: Linux and macOS reimagining of the Sysinternals ProcDump tool that writes process dumps in response to performance, runtime, signal and resource-tracking triggers, including native dumps through a Rust ELF writer and managed dumps through .NET diagnostics IPC.
requirements: Runs on Linux kernels 3.5+ or macOS Sierra+. Building needs stable Rust with rustfmt and clippy, plus Clang, pkg-config, libelf and zlib headers, gdb and gcore on Linux, or Xcode command-line tools, gdb and gcore on macOS. The macOS version has no resource tracking. Release 3.5.3 is from 2026-09-10.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: fishhook
resources.description: Small library that dynamically rebinds symbols in Mach-O binaries running on iOS, on device and in the simulator, by updating the lazy and non-lazy symbol pointers that dyld uses.
requirements: Used by adding fishhook.h and fishhook.c to a project.
BSD-3-Clause per LICENSE.

resources.name: pcode2code
resources.description: VBA p-code decompiler based on pcodedmp, written for Office documents whose macro source has been stomped to leave only bytecode. It takes a document or a previously saved pcodedmp dump and also works as a Python module.
requirements: Works with Python 2.6+ and Python 3.x and installs with pip along with pcodedmp.
GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.

resources.name: Weeping of the Empire: statically recompiling Tears of the Kingdom for Windows
resources.description: Weeping of the Empire builds a native Windows port of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom from the user's Switch game dump. It recompiles ARM64 code ahead of time to x86-64, supplies Switch services through a host runtime and renders through Vulkan. The engine documentation credits totk-recomp as the starting point and identifies the added Windows port, renderer, controls and menus.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 x64, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU driver and the user's game dump are required; encrypted dumps also require the user's keys. Installation needs internet access.
Game version 1.0.0 is supported, with 1.4.3 in beta; first visits may stutter while shaders are built.
MIT License.

resources.name: Exoproc
resources.description: Exoproc exposes Windows x64 process inspection and instrumentation to agents through a CLI and MCP server. It enumerates processes, reads and scans memory, installs function detours, redirects thread contexts and compiles C snippets for execution in a target process.
requirements: Live process instrumentation requires native Windows x64.
The Node.js route requires Node.js 18 or newer; the README also describes Bun and a standalone executable.
MIT License.

resources.name: GTA Mode: reverse-engineering SimCity 3000 Unlimited for a native plugin
resources.description: GTA Mode is a native plugin that adds direct control of spawned citizens and cars to SimCity 3000 Unlimited. It uses findings from Ghidra analysis of the game's binaries, GZCOM plugin loading, in-memory city structures and sprite archives. The C plugin runs in the original game, reads city data from its memory and decodes art from the user's installation; MODLOG.md records addresses, formats and dead ends.
requirements: A user's copy of SimCity 3000 Unlimited is required; the supported game DLLs are the Steam release's April 2000 builds.
Building requires a 32-bit mingw-w64 compiler; the HUD uses cnc-ddraw's OpenGL renderer.
The game's own traffic cannot yet be stolen and its own pedestrians cannot yet be punched; water does not block movement.
MIT License.

resources.name: FH2MP: reconstructed Forza Horizon 2 online services
resources.description: FH2MP restores Forza Horizon 2 multiplayer with a replacement server based on protocol behavior recovered from the Xbox One game client. An in-game shim redirects sockets and web-service calls, while Python and Go servers handle lobbies, worlds and online features; a launcher manages setup and updates.
requirements: A legitimately owned Forza Horizon 2 Xbox One build 1.0.0.64 and Azimuth are required.
The source warns of crashes, desynchronization and rough edges.
GPL-3.0 licence.

resources.name: OpenDeviceDB
resources.description: OpenDeviceDB indexes devices with existing firmware or protocol reverse-engineering work and links back to source projects. Its website lists installation routes and remaining vendor dependencies, while importers aggregate existing databases and an MCP server lets agents query device records.
requirements: Using the local website, importers or MCP server requires the repository's npm workflow.
Some device entries retain non-free vendor components or require vendor cloud services.
Code is AGPL-3.0-or-later; data is CC BY-SA 4.0.

resources.name: esp-idf-injection-ng
resources.description: esp-idf-injection-ng documents an investigation of ESP-IDF's compiled libnet80211.a frame-type check. The author traces why symbol overrides fail in v5 and later, then supplies an objcopy patch, demonstration firmware and captures for transmitting additional 802.11 management frames through esp_wifi_80211_tx.
requirements: An ESP-IDF installation and ESP32 hardware are needed for the demonstrated patch and firmware.
The author tested ESP-IDF v6.1-dev on classic ESP32; other listed versions and chips are conditional.
The patch changes the local ESP-IDF archive globally and affects builds using it.
MIT License.

resources.name: Cursed Lands: a Godot engine for Evil Islands and Lost in Astral
resources.description: Cursed Lands reimplements the engine for Evil Islands and Lost in Astral in Godot, reading maps, models, audio, scripts and tables from the player's own game copy. Its native rendering, combat, AI, scripting and interface systems follow the original game's rules, with releases for desktop, Android and browsers.
requirements: An owned copy of Evil Islands or Lost in Astral is required; the GOG base-game edition is the main tested version.
The browser version requires WebGL 2.
Apache License 2.0.

resources.name: pkg-to-anyps5
resources.description: pkg-to-anyps5 extracts PS5 debug game packages or game folders into the layout expected by the AnyPS5 relinker. It parses FIH, PFS and NAPS structures, decodes supported Kraken blocks, and unwraps fake-signed SELF executables and modules into ELF files.
requirements: Rust 1.88 or newer to build from source; input is a PS5 debug package or extracted game folder.
Retail packages, encrypted filesystems and encrypted SELF segments are refused; several Kraken entropy types are unimplemented.
GPL-3.0-or-later license.

resources.name: QuestPad: a USB gamepad from the Quest Touch radio protocol
resources.description: QuestPad implements the Quest Touch controllers' private 2.4 GHz radio protocol on nRF52840 firmware so a computer can use them as a USB gamepad. Its protocol reference documents pairing, AES-CCM encrypted controller packets, 2 ms link frames and input data; the firmware exposes generic gamepad, DS4 and XInput modes.
requirements: A Nordic nRF52840 Dongle or nice!nano v2 and Quest Touch controllers are required.
Python 3 is required for the control panel.
Quest 3/3S controllers and Linux support are listed as untested.
The repository provides MIT and Apache-2.0 licence files.

resources.name: PMCA-RE RELOADED
resources.description: PMCA-RE RELOADED is a Rust desktop and CLI toolkit for Sony cameras that includes experimental analysis of where menu settings reside in camera settings memory. It also parses firmware files, backup images and usage logs offline, and provides USB access to camera information, apps, firmware updates and settings. Supported operations depend on the camera generation.
requirements: Windows, macOS or Linux and a supported Sony camera connected by USB for device operations.
App installation, settings memory and function analysis require user-imported key material.
Function analysis is experimental; firmware flashing is reported on one camera and unconfirmed on other models.
MIT license.

resources.name: nfs-mw: a Rust reconstruction of Need for Speed: Most Wanted
resources.description: nfs-mw reconstructs Need for Speed: Most Wanted 2005 PC v1.3 in Rust using data read from the user's installation. Its format readers decode bChunk, JDLZ, HUFF, cars, textures, and the streamed city; the current runtime provides viewers, driving, menus, and free roam.
requirements: Rust stable and an installed copy of Need for Speed: Most Wanted PC v1.3 / Black Edition are required.
Windows and Linux are documented; gameplay beyond the listed menus and free roam remains on the roadmap.
Apache-2.0 and MIT license files are present.

resources.name: OSIRIS: replacing Onkyo receiver firmware through MCU protocol research
resources.description: OSIRIS replaces the DSP-board software of Onkyo TX-NR515 and TX-NR717 receivers with its own boot loader, Linux services and DSP code. The project documents the SPI exchange between the main MCU and DSP board, including 1032-byte transfers, frame structure and command meanings recovered from stock firmware and logs.
requirements: An Onkyo receiver with a D830 or OMAP-L137 DSP board; installation requires a DSP-board serial connection and BOOT-pin switching.
The README reports TX-NR717 working and TX-NR515 working with incomplete testing; DTS, Spotify, internet radio and DLNA are unfinished.
Original OSIRIS code is BSD-2-Clause; bundled upstream components retain the licenses stated in the README.

resources.name: Stadiacast: reconstructing the Stadia Controller's Wi-Fi service
resources.description: Stadiacast recreates the network service used by the Stadia Controller's Wi-Fi firmware so the controller can connect to a local computer. The receiver answers boot and discovery requests, completes WebRTC and DTLS sessions, decodes input and sends rumble commands. Protocol notes record findings from firmware reading and live controller runs, with protobuf schemas and receiver code in the repository.
requirements: A Stadia Controller with Wi-Fi firmware; the author tested ota.282115.
A Windows, macOS or Linux host on the controller's network; running from source requires Python 3.11+.
Linux needs root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to bind the required low ports.
MIT license.

resources.name: rust-deobf
resources.description: rust-deobf analyzes compiled, mainly Rust, ELF, PE and Mach-O binaries to recover hidden strings and related artifacts. It combines static call-site analysis with Unicorn function emulation, identifies Rust metadata and library functions, and offers unpacking and Ghidra annotations. CLI and MCP interfaces expose the core analysis; deeper control-flow and virtualization modules have separate licensing.
requirements: Python 3.10 or newer is specified for the core package.
The documented analysis covers x86-64, ARM64 and 32-bit x86 across ELF, PE and Mach-O.
The core is Apache-2.0; premium modules are dual-licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later or a commercial license.

resources.name: ThisFirmwareDoesNotExist
resources.description: ThisFirmwareDoesNotExist maps Arturia MicroFreak firmware 5.0.0.2084 and provides freakpatch to modify a user's official update file. Its notes cover the update format and firmware subsystems, while Ghidra scripts and assembly sources support the documented patch locations.
requirements: Python 3.11 or newer and the official MicroFreak 5.0.0.2084 .mff update file are required.
Some MIDI CC assignments may interfere with an untested stock function.
MIT license.

resources.name: RE-Workstation
resources.description: RE-Workstation is a Chinese reference library for reverse-engineering workflows and related security research. Its topic pages cover native binaries, APKs, firmware, JavaScript, patch diffing and malware analysis, with indexes, evidence templates and pattern references for locating relevant methods.
requirements: The full directory, including SKILL.md, CATALOG.md, knowledge/ and references/, is needed for agent-skill use.
Analysis tools are supplied by the host environment.
Original and newly organized content is GPL-3.0-only; third-party content retains its own terms.

resources.name: bf-private-server: a Brave Frontier revival server
resources.description: bf-private-server recreates a self-hosted server for Brave Frontier client version 2.19.6. Its C++23 service answers the game's HTTP requests, stores saves in SQLite and works with CDN workers and a patcher for the user's Android client; request tables and boot-flow notes document the protocol investigation. The server builds on an earlier emulator fork.
requirements: Git and Docker or a native C++23 toolchain are required for the server.
Game data and a copy of the Android client must be obtained separately.
Some client requests remain unimplemented and return a not-available response.
AGPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: Clickwill: reconstructing iPod library database editing
resources.description: Clickwill reconstructs direct editing of iPod classic and iPod nano music libraries in a Swift Mac app. It reads and writes iTunesDB and ArtworkDB on the device, preserves unknown record bytes, handles hash58 signatures and publishes a byte map that distinguishes measured fields from uncertain ones.
requirements: macOS 14 or later and an iPod classic or supported iPod nano for normal writing.
Building from source requires Xcode 27 and XcodeGen.
iPod nano third- and fourth-generation editing does not add new artwork until their formats are confirmed; other iPods open read-only by default.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: Virtual MPC Sample: rehosting Akai MPC Sample firmware in QEMU
resources.description: Virtual MPC Sample rehosts Akai MPC Sample 1.3.0.12 firmware in QEMU using a custom lab kernel and a browser panel for the device controls. The repository documents firmware and device architecture, emulates the panel's UART communication and provides a shell, tracing and mod testing against the user's own firmware files.
requirements: Requires the user's own MPC Sample 1.3.0.12 firmware partitions; the factory library additionally requires the user's own device.
Requires QEMU 9 or later, Docker for building, Python 3.9 or later and an OpenSSH client.
USB audio, other firmware versions and a Windows test run remain unfinished.
MIT licence, except Linux kernel patches under GPL-2.0.

resources.name: OpenJooki: replacing the Jooki 2 software and recovery path
resources.description: OpenJooki replaces the Jooki 2 music speaker's embedded Linux core and provides phone-based control, updates and SD-card recovery. Its technical notes map the device's Ingenic Linux and ESP32 split, storage partitions, Mender update slots and recovery behavior, while the repository contains the replacement Lua services and installer tooling.
requirements: A Jooki 2 device is the target hardware.
The replacement system is installed on the device's SD-card based embedded Linux environment.
MIT license.

resources.name: intel_ma
resources.description: intel_ma inspects PC management firmware in ME/TXE/CSME region images and full SPI dumps. Its Rust library and CLI parse partition tables, AMD PSP directories, UEFI firmware volumes and FIT records, and report Boot Guard, BIOS Guard and descriptor locks. It can also remove selected Intel ME components and set documented disable flags in an output image.
requirements: A compatible firmware region image or full SPI dump is required for image analysis.
The source lists x86_64 Linux and FreeBSD/amd64; live ME probing is Linux only.
AMD PSP support is inspection only.
GPL-3.0-or-later.

resources.name: breakinggood
resources.description: breakinggood captures a website's screenshots, cleaned DOM, computed design values, images, and XHR/fetch responses, then generates a Vite, React, and Tailwind rebuild with a mock API replaying observed JSON. Its CLI and MCP server expose site capture alongside a separate Git repository setup workflow.
requirements: Node 20 or newer and Git; website mode needs an installed Chrome or Edge browser and a configured model provider.
Pages behind logins, strong bot protection, or mostly rendered with canvas/WebGL may capture poorly.
MIT license.

resources.name: OpenLF2: a Little Fighter 2 engine reimplementation
resources.description: OpenLF2 reimplements Little Fighter 2 v2.0a as a playable C++ and Lua engine. It loads resources from the original game installer and provides local modes, replays, mods and network matches between OpenLF2 players. The author states that gameplay compatibility is still being refined.
requirements: The Little Fighter 2 v2.0a installer is needed for original game data; Flatpak downloads it during installation, while other platforms prompt users to provide a copy.
Building requires CMake 3.25+, Ninja, a C++23 compiler, and the development libraries listed in BUILDING.md.
Gameplay compatibility is still under development; original LF2 network compatibility is unsupported.
MIT license covers OpenLF2 code, scripts and documentation, not the original game assets.

resources.name: Stickwalker: porting Pokéwalker firmware to the Stick S3
resources.description: Stickwalker ports a matching reconstruction of Pokéwalker firmware to the M5Stack Stick S3. The repository includes firmware source, build tooling and placeholder artwork; users can build with artwork extracted from their own ROM, and a BPV10NF photodiode supplies infrared reception.
requirements: An M5Stack Stick S3, BPV10NF photodiode and USB-C data cable are specified.
Original graphics require artwork extracted from the user's own ROM; downloads use placeholder artwork.
MIT license.

resources.name: qemu-rtd2841
resources.description: qemu-rtd2841 adds a Realtek RTD2841/RTK284x TV machine model to QEMU for bare-metal diagnostics and local firmware experiments. Its board profile models AArch32 Cortex-A53 cores, GICv2, timers, SDHCI, Ethernet, UART, and a framebuffer, with diagnostic assembly and a staged test runner.
requirements: Build against the pinned QEMU revision with the RTD2841 patch and the documented host toolchain.
Linux boot requires a compatible local RTD2841 zImage and composite eMMC image.
The author reports that public tests cover bare-metal and synthetic storage tiers; full Android init and framework services remain open.
GPL-2.0 license.

resources.name: os-xgs-npu: reconstructing Sophos XGS coprocessor interfaces
resources.description: os-xgs-npu reconstructs interfaces to Sophos XGS appliance coprocessors through FreeBSD kernel modules and an OPNsense plugin. The work documents undocumented registers, PCIe device families and measured coprocessor behavior to expose front ports and offload firewall flows and IPsec associations.
requirements: Sophos XGS hardware and a matching OPNsense or FreeBSD environment; kernel modules are built on the appliance.
The author says the project is still being completed; two coprocessor families currently respond.
BSD-2-Clause license.

resources.name: Spark Mail: rehosting the Windows desktop app on Linux with Wine shims
resources.description: spark-mail-linux rehosts the Windows Spark Mail desktop app on Linux with Wine, two compatibility DLL shims and launcher scripts. The project documents application startup, browser authentication, notifications, clipboard and file-opening behavior, then patches specific DLL imports and bridges those functions to the Linux desktop.
requirements: An official Windows Spark.exe installer, Wine, and Arch Linux or an Arch-based system as documented.
The author reports that Spark 3.32.2.141404 starts; mail, calendar, attachment and notification delivery checks remain incomplete for that version.
MIT licence.

resources.name: LibreMP: an Epson EasyMP screen caster from packet-capture research
resources.description: LibreMP casts desktop screens to Epson EasyMP projectors using a protocol reconstructed from Windows client packet captures. Its Rust core handles registration and login messages, projector QR decoding, JPEG tile streaming and changed-region updates; a CLI and Tauri interface use the same core. The project documents control on TCP 3620 and video on TCP 3621.
requirements: An Epson EasyMP-compatible projector and a supported desktop operating system; building requires Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, NASM and CMake.
The keyword-protected login path has not been tried against real hardware; Windows and macOS casting still need hardware testing.
MIT License.

resources.name: CFG Visualizer
resources.description: CFG Visualizer extracts function control-flow graphs from ELF, PE and Mach-O binaries with radare2 and presents them in an interactive 3D browser view. Its FastAPI backend returns graph JSON, while the frontend shows branch edges and node disassembly.
requirements: Python 3.10+ and radare2 on PATH are required for local binary analysis.
The public upload service lacks authentication, rate limiting and subprocess sandboxing.
MIT.

resources.name: Atlantis Native: porting the Atlantis and Atlantis II engines to Rust
resources.description: Atlantis Native ports the reverse-engineered CryOmni3D Atlantis engine to Rust for Atlantis: The Lost Tales and Atlantis II. It reads files from the user's own game copies and runs their scripts, panoramas, cinematics and puzzles on desktop systems and in browsers, with optional display and bug fixes.
requirements: Users supply their own copies of Atlantis: The Lost Tales or Atlantis II; game data is not included.
Desktop builds cover Windows, macOS and Linux; a browser build is also described.
GPL-3.0-or-later license.

resources.name: Sony CDX-A250: reconstructing the LCD panel interface
resources.description: Sony CDX-A250 LCD Panel reconstructs the serial control needed to drive the radio's detachable display independently through its LC75826W driver. Wiring notes, CCB transfer documentation, and an Arduino sketch cover display-data groups, control bits, test patterns, and experimental segment mapping.
requirements: The documented setup uses a Sony CDX-A250 front panel, an Arduino-compatible board, bench power, a pushbutton, and wiring components.
The project documents the demonstrated panel setup and the LC75826W interface used by its Arduino sketch.
Code is MIT licensed; original documentation and project media are CC BY 4.0.

resources.name: apkscope
resources.description: apkscope inspects Android application packages through a Rust viewer, CLI, and MCP server. It decompiles DEX classes into Java, searches code and references, reads manifests and resources, scans URLs and secrets including native libraries, and can export or modify packages.
requirements: Supply an Android application package such as an APK or XAPK.
Apache-2.0 license.

resources.name: MacroPad: reconstructing a USB macropad configuration protocol
resources.description: MacroPad reconstructs the USB HID configuration exchange of a 12-key, two-knob macropad identified as 1189:8840 and implements it in a Linux GUI. The author documents capturing MINI_KEYBOARD.exe traffic with usbmon, decoding configuration and commit reports, and replaying captured packets in tests.
requirements: Linux, Python 3.9+ and the 1189:8840 macropad are documented for the supported configuration path.
Other pad IDs are reported as unsupported until their layout and protocol are added.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: Monix: reconstructing Audient iD USB mixer control on Linux
resources.description: Monix implements Linux mixer control for Audient iD USB audio interfaces through a companion kernel module, protocol library and GUI. Its protocol documentation maps USB control requests from official-app captures and macOS binary analysis, covering routing, faders, metering and device profiles.
requirements: Requires Linux kernel 5.9 or newer and an Audient iD-series interface.
Building requires a C++17 toolchain, CMake 3.16 or newer, kernel headers, ALSA, GLFW and OpenGL development packages.
The author reports hardware testing on iD24; other models have limited or unconfirmed routing support.
MIT license.

resources.name: SF2Recomp: statically recompiling Shadow Fight 2 for native platforms
resources.description: SF2Recomp converts a user's Shadow Fight 2 Nintendo Switch game files into native builds for Linux, Windows, macOS, and Android. Its converter combines translated game code with a runtime and user-supplied assets, adding controls, graphics options, sparring, and LAN play.
requirements: Supply a combined base plus v1.1.0/update v131072 NSP with sidecars and prod.keys, or already extracted updated game files.
A Vulkan 1.3 compatible GPU and driver are required; platform version requirements vary.
macOS Apple Silicon support is experimental, with gameplay and GPU validation pending.
Project code is MIT licensed; dependencies and the project icon have separate terms.

resources.name: Scooter Link: a Xiaomi scooter client built from BLE protocol research
resources.description: Scooter Link implements an Android client for Xiaomi Electric Scooter 5 Pro and 5 Max using a reconstructed BLE authentication protocol. Its research log covers GATT characteristics and investigation of the ECDH P-256, HKDF-SHA256, and AES-CCM exchange; the app reads ride and battery data and controls supported settings.
requirements: Android and a supported Xiaomi Electric Scooter; the author reports testing the 5 Pro and 5 Max.
Other listed models have experimental read-only support or remain untested.
PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0.

resources.name: sony-bravia-linux: pre-Android BRAVIA platform and media behavior
resources.description: sony-bravia-linux investigates the Linux-based, pre-Android Sony BRAVIA platform and reconstructs selected media and portal behavior for owner-run services. Its documentation records observations from 2011–2012 AZ1, AZ2 and AZ3 sets, including remote input, browser media handling and 3D signalling. The repository also contains tools for H.264 3D SEI and related media workflows.
requirements: The documented platform scope is 2011–2012 pre-Android Sony BRAVIA AZ1, AZ2 and AZ3 chassis families.
The author reports testing media behavior on two owned TVs.
The main LICENSE file is GPL-2.0; the README also identifies separate licences for parts of the repository.

resources.name: dfsdk
resources.description: dfsdk dumps Delta Force object metadata by enumerating its object array, decoding per-entry XOR-encrypted names and walking class super chains and property lists. The README documents name-pool addressing, pointer masking, selected field offsets and example output.
requirements: A Delta Force process with the documented object and name-pool layout is the target input.
The documented offsets are specific to the investigated layout.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Sound Blaster AE-9: reconstructing Linux control from Windows driver analysis
resources.description: Sound Blaster AE-9 Linux support reconstructs card and Audio Control Module behavior using static analysis of Creative's Windows drivers and hardware observations. The included investigations document CtxHda.sys, CtxHdb.sys, and the ACM's SysEx-framed UART protocol; the driver implements selected playback and controls.
requirements: Linux kernel 6.17 or newer, headers, DKMS, build tools, PipeWire, and WirePlumber are specified.
A Creative driver package is needed to extract a DSP firmware segment locally.
The author reports support for 7 of 16 listed features across the card and Audio Control Module; recording is disabled because opening capture hard-locked the test machine.
GPL-2.0 license.

resources.name: KBot
resources.description: KBot inspects and transforms Total Annihilation and TA: Kingdoms game files, pairing a Go CLI with a proprietary format reference. It decompiles COB bytecode to BOS source, disassembles scripts, checks round trips and examines formats including HPI archives, GAF sprites, TNT maps and 3DO models.
requirements: Go is needed to install or build the CLI.
Asset inspection requires files from Total Annihilation or TA: Kingdoms; an installed game can provide them.
MIT license.

resources.name: thermalmaster: a Go client for ThermalMaster camera USB commands
resources.description: thermalmaster implements a Go USB client for ThermalMaster P3 and P1 thermal cameras using documented VDCMD control transfers. It captures PNG frames, streams thermal and IR video to Linux v4l2loopback, and records USB command framing and model identifiers for interoperability.
requirements: A ThermalMaster P3 or P1 camera, a C toolchain, pkg-config and libusb development files.
Linux with v4l2loopback is required for video streaming; USB permissions must be configured.
CC0-1.0 license.

resources.name: Cpp2CS
resources.description: Cpp2CS recovers managed methods from Android ARM64 Unity IL2CPP ELF binaries and matching metadata, emitting CIL assemblies, C# source and per-method diagnostics. Its pipeline models machine IR, IL2CPP runtime idioms, memory SSA and type recovery while marking unresolved portions.
requirements: .NET 10 SDK, the Il2CppDumper submodule, and a matching binary and metadata pair.
Recovery is modeled for Android ARM64 ELF, Unity 2022.3.62f2 and metadata v31.
Generated project files do not establish that the source compiles or runs.
MIT license.

resources.name: ghidra-c6000
resources.description: ghidra-c6000 adds Texas Instruments C64x, C67x and C674x DSP support to Ghidra 12.x. Its SLEIGH languages decode full-width and compact instructions, supply p-code for decompilation, and add C6000 calling conventions and packet-aware analyzers for ELF or raw images.
requirements: Requires a matching Ghidra 12.x build and its declared JDK: JDK 21 for Ghidra 12.0 or 12.1, JDK 25 for 12.2.
Raw images require a chosen base address and entry point.
C66x-specific instructions and complete C66x ISA support are absent.
Apache-2.0 license.

resources.name: Sheypoor MCP: mapping marketplace APIs from browser traffic
resources.description: Sheypoor MCP implements a client and MCP server for the Sheypoor classifieds site using API behavior documented from browser traffic. Its reference records observed endpoints, request headers, cookies and phone-based login. The server exposes listing search and details, account functions, chat room lists and unread message counts to MCP clients.
requirements: Node.js 20.11+ is indicated for the MCP server.
Account features require Sheypoor phone and SMS authentication.
MIT License.

resources.name: open-rknpu: Rockchip NPU task-program reconstruction
resources.description: open-rknpu reconstructs a task-program interface for the Rockchip RV1103/RV1106 NPU from board experiments and black-box comparisons. Its Python compiler emits register commands, weight and quantization blocks, and a container for bounded static ONNX convolution graphs; a C runtime submits them through /dev/rknpu. Research files document register and numerical findings.
requirements: Host compilation needs Python, NumPy and ONNX; hardware runs need a compatible board and cross toolchain.
The reference board is a Luckfox Pico Mini B with the shared RV1106 NPU IP and driver v0.8.2.
Dynamic shapes, LSTM/GRU, 1-D convolution, MatMul/Gemm and multi-stage detection heads are outside the documented scope.
MIT license for the compiler, runtime, tests, examples and documentation.

resources.name: Devil May Cry: an experimental PS2 static recompilation
resources.description: dmc-recomp translates the PlayStation 2 PAL release of Devil May Cry into native PC code through PS2Recomp and a project runtime. Its pipeline rebuilds generated code locally from the user’s own game executable, while research notes and patches track boot, CD services, MPEG playback, rendering and gameplay behavior.
requirements: A user-supplied copy of the PAL Europe Devil May Cry version 1.02 executable or disc image.
PS2Recomp at the pinned upstream commit and the documented build toolchain.
The source describes the port as experimental, with incomplete rendering and gameplay.
GPL-3.0 licence.

resources.name: hardsid4u: reconstructing the HardSID 4U USB protocol
resources.description: hardsid4u reconstructs the HardSID 4U USB protocol and implements a libusb Python driver for its SID-chip sockets. The investigation combines vendor-binary analysis, USB captures, and hardware probes to document command framing, initialization, register writes, timing, and flow control; a MIDI instrument uses the driver.
requirements: A HardSID 4U device is needed for hardware use; the core driver requires Python 3.9+, libusb1, and libusb.
MIDI output additionally uses python-rtmidi and CoreMIDI as documented.
The author reports that a stalled device may require a physical power cycle; isochronous mode and SID file playback are unused or absent.
MIT license.

resources.name: MS4X
resources.description: MS4X analyzes Siemens MS42 and MS43 engine-control firmware for BMW M52TU and M54 engines. Its Python tools disassemble and assemble C166 instructions and inspect image checksums, stock-code differences and TunerPro patchlists; companion documents cover memory maps and findings in the factory programs.
requirements: Python 3 and a user-supplied MS42 or MS43 image.
New material is paused; the author says error reports are still addressed.
Code is Apache-2.0; documents and data are CC BY-SA 4.0.

resources.name: ZCode-Android: reconstructing the ZCode remote-control client
resources.description: ZCode-Android recreates ZCode remote control on Android from captured traffic and analysis of its official web page. Its Kotlin client implements WebSocket relay, HMAC pairing, IPC encoding, fragmented RPC frames and Conversation V4 session messages.
requirements: Android 12+ on arm64-v8a and a desktop ZCode pairing link are required.
Building requires JDK 17 and Android SDK 35.
Changes to the official web protocol may break the client.
The README declares an MIT licence.

resources.name: PyEilik: a client for the Eilik robot's USB protocol
resources.description: PyEilik implements control of an Eilik desk robot over a recovered USB serial protocol. Its C library and Python wrapper move four servos, read and update the 128×64 display, and play video with synchronized movement. The protocol reference documents 125000-baud framing, command IDs, checksums and acknowledgements.
requirements: macOS and Python 3.9 or newer are required; the serial link uses an Apple-specific ioctl for 125000 baud.
Video playback requires ffmpeg on PATH; PNG display requires the image extra.
The robot's speaker cannot receive audio through the documented protocol.
MIT license.

resources.name: libfprint-goodixtls: a reconstructed Goodix GXFP5187 fingerprint driver
resources.description: libfprint-goodixtls reconstructs communication with the Goodix GXFP5187 SPI fingerprint sensor in the Huawei MateBook X Pro as a libfprint TOD driver. It reads a PSK from sensor RAM, establishes the sensor's TLS-PSK channel, decodes captured images, and uses local descriptors for host-side matching. The author reports enrolment and verification through fprintd and GNOME Settings; detailed reverse-engineering notes are kept outside the repository.
requirements: Goodix GXFP5187 sensor on the Huawei MateBook X Pro MACH-WX9, with a usable spidev node.
The detailed protocol-frame and matching-engine notes are kept separately from the repository.
Matcher error rates in the README are author-reported results from the described capture sets.
LGPL-2.1 License.

resources.name: Walksnail Ascent VRX UART Protocol
resources.description: Walksnail Ascent VRX UART Protocol documents serial control messages for Walksnail video receivers and supplies a C reference transmitter with an STM32 example. It specifies framing, payload checksums, remote keys, channel selection and status queries, while recording contradictions and unknown reply layouts.
requirements: A Walksnail VRX and a controller with a compatible UART interface for hardware use.
The library limits payloads to 64 bytes; baud rate, electrical levels and pinout need hardware confirmation.
TX examples are tested against supplied documentation; RX telemetry layout and device behavior remain unresolved.
MIT license.

resources.name: Sin & Punishment: a work-in-progress N64 static recompilation
resources.description: Sin & Punishment: Recompiled uses N64Recomp and RSPRecomp to build an experimental native C++ port from a user-supplied Japanese N64 ROM and the repository's symbol maps, with RT64 rendering. The author reports that it reaches the title screen; menu navigation, gameplay, audio validation, and a public pipeline for its patched working image remain unfinished.
requirements: A legally obtained Japanese Sin & Punishment ROM, Python 3, the pinned submodules, and the platform build toolchain described in the README.
The current recompilation configuration also expects a patched working image whose preparation pipeline is absent from the public repository.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: scvk: replacing SimCity 4's renderer with Vulkan
resources.description: scvk reconstructs SimCity 4's renderer interface as a native Vulkan DLL loaded through the game's GZCOM plugin system. It claims existing renderer class IDs and emulates the cIGZGDriver fixed-function API with pipeline state and shaders for terrain, buildings, lighting, textures and interface drawing.
requirements: SimCity 4 with the documented GZCOM plugin interface and Vulkan-capable graphics hardware.
SCGL cannot be installed concurrently because it claims the same renderer class ID; Intel graphics are untested.
LGPL-2.1-or-later license.

resources.name: RazerStream: reconstructing Stream Controller device control
resources.description: RazerStream replaces the retired control software for the Razer Stream Controller with a macOS app, Swift protocol library and CLI. Its documented device protocol runs over a USB serial port, performs a WebSocket upgrade, then exchanges framed commands and input events. The app configures touchscreen tiles, knobs, buttons and LEDs.
requirements: macOS 14 or newer and a Razer Stream Controller with USB VID 0x1532 and PID 0x0D06.
Xcode 16 or newer to build from source; Accessibility permission is needed for keystroke and media-key actions.
The app targets macOS only.
MIT license.

resources.name: DABplay+: reconstructing USB DAB+ dongle control
resources.description: DABplay+ implements an Android DAB radio using a reverse-engineered USB dongle protocol. It drives the DTR-100 family directly, decodes broadcast data and audio, and documents additional dongle protocols alongside hardware findings and tests.
requirements: Android 8+ and a supported USB DAB+ dongle are required.
Building requires JDK 25 and the Android SDK.
Only the first listed dongle family has been tested on real hardware; several on-air features remain unconfirmed.
MIT.

resources.name: T2 platform research
resources.description: T2 platform research maps Apple T2 firmware, hardware and Linux-facing interfaces using static analysis, hardware observations and driver comparisons. Its chapters cover Secure Enclave services, boot and recovery, graphics, audio, sensors, storage and other subsystems. Machine-readable findings and board indexes connect claims to their evidence, with Python reference code for selected message formats.
requirements: The main firmware inventory covers bridgeOS 23P6068 across 16 production configurations.
Most host observations concern MacBookPro16,1 / J152fAP; other board and firmware claims have separate scope.
The reference code does not provide a driver or fingerprint service.
MIT license.

resources.name: PocketPrinter5890: reconstructing the Lidl 5890 printer protocol
resources.description: PocketPrinter5890 reconstructs the BLE printing protocol of Lidl's Tronic, SILVERCREST, and Parkside model 5890 pocket printers. Its specification documents activation writes, flow-control credits, and raster bands; Swift, Kotlin, and TypeScript libraries implement printing for Apple devices, Android, and browsers.
requirements: The documented reference device is model A2Y with firmware V1.06LY; other revisions may differ.
The browser demo requires Web Bluetooth in Chrome, Edge, or Opera.
Firmware updating is not implemented, and roughly twenty transcribed commands were not executed on the reference firmware.
MIT license.

resources.name: Salamander UEFI: a disassembly-based UEFI port of the NES game
resources.description: Salamander UEFI ports the NES game Salamander to a native UEFI Shell application by translating its 6502 disassembly into a platform-independent C core. The repository includes a 6502 disassembler, a user-ROM resource extractor, host tests and a fidelity checklist. UEFI GOP, input and timing services replace the original console environment.
requirements: A legally held Salamander NES ROM is required to generate game-resource headers.
Building requires Windows, Visual Studio 2019, EDK2 and Python 3.10 or newer; QEMU/OVMF is used for emulated runs.
The app has no audio, and the source lists score display and some boss sprite differences.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: cocos2d-dumper
resources.description: cocos2d-dumper extracts defined function symbols from ELF shared libraries and demangles C++ names with GNU binutils. It produces a map of ELF symbol values and names for inspecting unstripped cocos2d-x binaries and other native libraries.
requirements: Python 3.9 or newer and GNU binutils readelf and c++filt are required.
Unstripped libraries provide the usable function symbols described by the tool.
MIT license.

resources.name: Binary Ninja Security Analysis Plugin
resources.description: Binary Ninja Security Analysis Plugin batches binary analysis from a Rust plugin and exports Parquet reports. It records architecture, hashes, functions, strings, segments, cyclomatic complexity, entropy and references to selected process-execution functions.
requirements: Requires Binary Ninja, a stable Rust toolchain and Binary Ninja API development headers.
The author reports testing the rebuilt command in Binary Ninja Personal 6.1.10951-dev.
MIT License.

resources.name: NWBinAnalyzer
resources.description: NWBinAnalyzer inspects compiled NW.js .bin files by checking their header and walking constant-pool entries. Its Python code extracts UTF-8, null-terminated and length-prefixed strings, then groups findings such as API names, paths, URLs and cryptographic terms.
requirements: Python 3.6+; the author says the tool uses only the standard library.
The author states that it shows constant-pool strings and does not fully decompile V8 bytecode.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Parking sensor kit: reconstructing its display protocol
resources.description: This parking-sensor investigation reconstructs the signal sent from a kit's controller to its display. Oscilloscope observations and tests with different sensor states identify fields in roughly 48-bit frames for sensor address, connection and proximity. A PlatformIO example for ATmega328P reads and reports the parsed frames.
requirements: The example targets an ATmega328P microcontroller and a compatible parking-sensor kit.
Controller electronics vary across similar kits, so the code may need changes.
Check signal voltage before connecting a microcontroller; the documented unit exceeded 5 V.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Glaurung Models
resources.description: Glaurung Models contains tokenizer and model experiments for executable analysis. Its documented 64K BPE tokenizer encodes compiled PE and ELF bytes using Latin-1, with x86 and ARM64 training coverage; an accompanying analysis compares learned SSE and AVX instruction patterns across two tokenizers.
requirements: The documented tokenizer workflow uses the tokenizers and transformers Python packages and Latin-1 conversion of binary bytes.
The document reports an average of 2.849 bytes per token for the 64K tokenizer.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: pyhaseiq: reconstructing the older Hase iQ stove's WebSocket protocol
resources.description: pyhaseiq reconstructs the local WebSocket protocol of Hase iQ wood stoves used with the flamemonitor app and implements an asynchronous read-only Python client. The specification records base64-encoded request and response frames, serial dialogue and observation status for each finding; the client reads combustion phase, temperature and performance.
requirements: Python 3.13 or newer and a supported flamemonitor-generation Hase iQ stove on the local network.
The newer HASE iQ app generation is unsupported; the API is described as alpha.
The library implements no write commands.
MIT license.

resources.name: CrackMes
resources.description: CrackMes is a set of walkthroughs for purpose-built crackme binaries from crackmes.one. The supplied Linux x86-64 examples identify ELF executables, inspect program disassembly, use breakpoints and runtime observations, and explain how candidate input is checked.
requirements: The covered examples use Linux x86-64 crackme binaries obtained separately from crackmes.one.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Human-Readable Decompilation
resources.description: Human-Readable Decompilation restructures C produced by Ghidra's binary decompiler using an ANTLR parser and AST transformations. It recovers switches from conditional chains, introduces guard clauses, flattens nested branches and simplifies selected expressions. A GUI can launch Ghidra headlessly before transformation, while a CLI handles existing C output.
requirements: Ghidra 11.4.2 or later, a Java runtime and Python 3 are specified for the full workflow.
ANTLR Python runtime and tools are needed to generate the parser.
Further transformation coverage, including iteration statements, remains planned.
BSD-3-Clause license.

resources.name: BinStruct Inspector
resources.description: BinStruct Inspector is a GUI for examining binary file layouts through user-defined field trees. It parses files as structures are edited, shows parsed values beside synchronized hex and JSON views, and tracks byte-level insertions, deletions, and replacements; plugins add custom data types.
requirements: The package manifest requires Python 3.11+ and PySide6 6.0+.
MIT license.

resources.name: SimpleParserPE
