resources.description: SimpleParserPE is a C++ command-line inspector for PE32 Windows executables. It reads DOS and NT headers, section metadata, data directories, and imported DLL functions, translating RVAs through the section table without Windows headers or external libraries.
requirements: A C++17 compiler and a PE32 executable input are required.
PE32+ is rejected; bounds checking is absent, and exports, relocations, and resources are not parsed.
MIT license.

resources.name: BNDExtract
resources.description: BNDExtract is a Go command-line tool for extracting the ALL.BND archive used by Kuon and some other FromSoftware PlayStation 2 games. It takes a .bnd file and an output directory, providing access to the archive's contents for inspection.
requirements: A supported .bnd archive and Go to build the tool.
The documented support centres on Kuon's ALL.BND and some other FromSoftware PS2 releases.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: tenet_tracer
resources.description: tenet_tracer uses Intel Pin to record instruction-level execution traces for Tenet. It captures program counters, register changes and memory accesses, stores them in SQLite tables, and provides a script to export the trace text.
requirements: Intel Pin is required; the documented Windows build uses Visual Studio 2022 and Pin 3.31 with LLVM clang-cl.
Kernel debugging must be disabled for the documented Pin setup.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Binary BPE Tokenizer for Executable Analysis
resources.description: Binary BPE Tokenizer for Executable Analysis studies byte-pair encoding of ELF, PE, Mach-O and APK files for transformer-based binary analysis. The repository provides paper sources, 4K to 64K tokenizer vocabularies, Python evaluation scripts and a sample archive. The author reports 2.89 bytes per token for the 64K vocabulary.
requirements: Python 3.10+ with uv; TeX Live 2023+ is required to compile the paper.
Rust 1.70+ is optional for retraining the tokenizer from scratch.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Power BI API Scraper: decoding a published report query format
resources.description: Power BI API Scraper reconstructs the web client's undocumented query and response format for published reports. It sends SemanticQueryDataShapeCommand requests, follows restart tokens and expands bitsets and ValueDicts into CSV rows. The included example is hardcoded for an Ohio liquor permit report.
requirements: Python 3.7+ and requests; access to a public Power BI report.
The included query, resource key and model ID are hardcoded for one report; retargeting requires code changes.
Non-200 responses stop the run, and overlapping pages are not deduplicated.
MIT License.

resources.name: m0rph: tracing an obfuscated ELF flag checker
resources.description: The m0rph investigation examines an obfuscated x86-64 ELF CTF flag checker with readelf, strings, Cutter and Radare2. Its write-up traces indirect CALL RAX execution into allocated memory and describes recovering expected characters by breaking at the call and inspecting RDI during each loop iteration.
requirements: The m0rph x86-64 ELF challenge binary and a Linux analysis environment are needed to repeat the investigation.
Radare2, Cutter and standard Linux inspection utilities are used in the described workflow.
MIT license.

resources.name: OpenTracks: a UWP port of OpenTracks7 BETA1
resources.description: OpenTracks is an early UWP port of the OpenTracks7 BETA1 Windows Phone music app informed by the author's reverse engineering. Its C# and XAML implementation updates page control access and replaces WP7 MediaPlayerLauncher with UWP media playback APIs.
requirements: Targets Windows 10 Mobile; the project uses Windows SDK 19041 with minimum SDK 10240.
The author describes the port as pre-beta, with settings storage, playback behavior and background tasks still needing work.
MIT license.

resources.name: BinScan
resources.description: BinScan scans files in bulk and emits per-file JSON containing format identification, structural metadata, hashes and entropy. Its C++ library includes parsers for PE, ELF and Mach-O executables alongside archives, packages, documents and images, with a staged read, analyze and write pipeline.
requirements: C++20, CMake and OpenSSL; the README provides Windows, Linux and macOS build instructions.
The author describes the current version as unreleased and warns that results may contain inaccuracies.
MIT license.

resources.name: Patch-0xC0000022
resources.description: Patch-0xC0000022 instruments the running Windows SysMain service by changing its NtCreateFile response to STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED. The C++ program finds the service process, resolves the remote function address and applies a six-byte patch to study the effect on prefetch behavior.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 x64, Visual Studio C++ tools and administrator permission are required.
The source calls for a controlled test environment and says restarting Windows restores runtime state.
Restoring or removing the patch is listed as future work.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: LED Controller: a BanlanX BLE client with audio-feed protocol findings
resources.description: LED Controller uses BanlanX BLE commands to control SP611E-family LED strips from a desktop app. Its documentation maps GATT commands and state notifications, and reports probing an audio-feed message used by the controller’s music effects; included tools inspect advertisements, GATT state and Bluetooth captures.
requirements: A PC with Bluetooth Low Energy, uv and a compatible BanlanX controller.
PC audio input works on Windows only; BanlanX v3 models are implemented from UniLED documentation but untested on hardware.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: CPQ IO Scheduler: reconstructing Xiaomi's block scheduler
resources.description: CPQ IO Scheduler reconstructs Xiaomi's proprietary cpq.ko Linux block scheduler from a stripped ARM64 kernel module. Its out-of-tree C implementation combines priority classes, thread-group queues, deadline handling, and blk-mq elevator integration, with a whitepaper and author-reported benchmarks.
requirements: Building requires Linux kernel headers for the block layer and scheduler APIs; the author reports testing on Linux 6.1 with RK3588 and eMMC 5.1.
The author reports a 5-of-6 workload win against mq-deadline, with about 1.9% average IOPS uplift.
GPL-2.0 license, as stated in the README and source-file notice.

resources.name: Zemismart Blind Controller Protocol: RF command reconstruction
resources.description: Zemismart Blind Controller Protocol documents the 433.92 MHz OOK PWM messages used by Zemismart motorized blind remotes. It records pulse timing, payload fields and formulas for channel and button commands, with Python scripts to capture IQ samples and encode or decode transmissions.
requirements: Zemismart motorized blind remote captures; the capture script uses LimeSDR and SoapySDR.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: RE4METoolbox
resources.description: RE4METoolbox provides command-line utilities for examining and modifying Resident Evil 4 Mobile Edition files. RE4MEAcvTool unpacks and repacks ACV .bin archives, while RE4METextTool converts Mission and Resource .bin text files to TSV and repacks edited text.
requirements: Resident Evil 4 Mobile Edition .bin files; the text tool requires a Mission or Resource format flag.
MIT license.

resources.name: AC46 Firmware Tool
resources.description: AC46 Firmware Tool unpacks firmware images for JieLi AC4600/BT15 devices. It accepts a dumped flash image or a BFU file with its first 512 bytes removed, detects an encryption state, extracts bootloader and resource files, and writes a repacking batch script. The repository also lists cipher, CRC16, and chip-key utilities.
requirements: A flash image from a JieLi AC46/BT15 device, or a BFU file with its first 512 bytes removed, is required.
Repacking requires an AC46 SDK.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: iMonitor
resources.description: iMonitor is a Windows endpoint activity monitor for examining running software. It records process, file, registry and network events, adds DLL-load analysis, and supports custom columns and matching rules through plugins and scripts.
requirements: Windows is required.
MIT license.

resources.name: RTO eChalan: investigating a BankBot Android APK
resources.description: The RTO eChalan report investigates an Android APK impersonating an Indian government eChallan service through manifest review, JADX decompilation and sandbox analysis. The author reports identifying a BankBot variant, a REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES permission, a BIND_VPN_SERVICE entry and extensive obfuscation that limited decompilation.
requirements: The report covers one Android APK named RTO eChalan.apk.
The author reports that approximately 96% of classes failed to load during decompilation.
CC-BY-4.0 license.

resources.name: m68kdasm
resources.description: m68kdasm disassembles Motorola 68000-family machine code in Go and returns assembly with structured instruction metadata. It supports selectable CPU variants, optional FPU and PMMU decoding, symbol and label formatting, streaming input and helpers for 68000 ELF binaries.
requirements: Go 1.27, as specified in go.mod.
Some CPU instructions, including CPU32 TBLS/TBLU and 68040 MOVE16/CINV/CPUSH, remain unimplemented.
MIT license.

resources.name: Malware Analysis: njRAT and Casdet behavior investigation
resources.description: A malware investigation examines njRAT and a UPX-packed Casdet executable with PEStudio static triage and ANY.RUN sandbox telemetry, alongside a malicious PDF and benign comparison files. The author reports process, registry and network behavior, extracted indicators and MITRE ATT&CK mappings in a report and screenshots.
requirements: The investigation used PEStudio 9.56 and ANY.RUN on a Windows 10 guest.
The author reports that Infected.exe crashed because libelf.dll was missing, so no sandbox behavior was observed for it.

resources.name: IR Lifting Benchmark
resources.description: IR Lifting Benchmark compares binary lifting workflows across Ghidra P-code, angr VEX, BAP BIL and optional LLVM IR paths. Shell and Python scripts run analyses on binary samples, collect performance and control-flow metrics, check lifted semantics and generate reports and visualizations.
requirements: Linux, Python 3.8 or later, Ghidra 10.x or 11.x and the selected analysis tools.
BAP and LLVM lifting are optional; true binary-to-LLVM IR lifting needs RetDec or llvm-mctoll.
User-provided samples are needed for malware analysis.
MIT license.

resources.name: OpenOCD SPI Dump Plugin
resources.description: OpenOCD SPI Dump Plugin guides an agent through extracting SPI flash or EEPROM contents using a target MCU's SWD/JTAG debug connection. It supplies MCU register maps, a RAM-resident C reader, linker and OpenOCD Tcl templates, and a workflow for JEDEC identification and dump checking.
requirements: OpenOCD, an ARM GNU toolchain, and netcat are required.
A working SWD/JTAG probe connection and an MCU connected to SPI flash or EEPROM are required.
The maximum dump chunk size remains to be parameterized.
MIT license.

resources.name: Bin-Hunter
resources.description: Bin-Hunter is a Python command-line tool for initial static inspection of binary files. It identifies formats from magic bytes, calculates whole-file and peak-region Shannon entropy, extracts readable strings, and finds URLs, IP addresses, email addresses, and suspicious keywords in those strings.
requirements: Python standard library; no external dependencies are stated.
MIT license.

resources.name: vanmoof-certificates: decoding VanMoof bike certificates
resources.description: vanmoof-certificates decodes the access certificates used with VanMoof SA5 and Series 6 bikes. It documents an Ed25519 signature followed by a CBOR payload containing bike serials, user identity, access role and expiry, and provides Go code to request, parse and check certificates. The source says the SA5 verification key was recovered from a bike BLE certificate.
requirements: A VanMoof account with a supported bike is needed to request certificates.
The source states that the Series 6 signing key is not yet known, so its signatures are not verified.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Aspyr Archive Tool
resources.description: Aspyr Archive Tool unpacks and rebuilds Android OBB archives used by three Aspyr game ports: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II, Jade Empire: Special Edition and Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy Remastered. Its command-line options support full or selective compression and a CRC64 checksum for Jade Empire.
requirements: An OBB archive from one of the listed games is required.
MIT.

resources.name: BinaryInsight
resources.description: BinaryInsight inspects ELF, PE, and Mach-O executables and libraries in an interactive terminal view or a text-report CLI. Its Rust core uses goblin to parse binary structure and exposes sections, symbols, printable strings, and security mitigation indicators such as PIE, NX, RELRO, ASLR, and DEP.
requirements: Rust and Cargo are required to build from source.
MIT License.

resources.name: ScriptSource-Dumper
resources.description: ScriptSource-Dumper extracts scripts from Call of Duty: Black Ops II scriptsrc.clump archives. Its C++ parser reads the archive table of contents and data chunks, locates the internal name table, and writes files under their recovered names and directories.
requirements: A scriptsrc.clump archive from Call of Duty: Black Ops II.
Visual Studio 2022 or newer and the MSVC v145 toolset to build.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: derkt
resources.description: derkt parses and disassembles Hermes Bytecode files in Racket. It decodes HBC structures and function data, detects the bytecode version and loads a matching generated instruction definition before producing disassembly. The repository includes versioned ISA definitions, parsers and a sample HBC file.
requirements: Racket is required; the CLI accepts an HBC file path.
MIT.

resources.name: .AUP-File-Type-Decryptor-and-Viewer
resources.description: .AUP-File-Type-Decryptor-and-Viewer is a local browser tool for inspecting Dragon Soul .aup game asset files. It implements the documented LZSS variant, previews image, audio and text formats, and exports files while preserving folder structure. The README specifies the four-byte size header and ring-buffer command stream.
requirements: A browser and Dragon Soul .aup files are required for use.
Encoding and compression of raw files back into .aup is listed as unfinished.
MIT license.

resources.name: ODIS file unpacker
resources.description: ODIS file unpacker extracts protected Java classes from ODIS plugin JARs and files from its DIDB data archives. The author traces AES class decryption and Blowfish ECB data decryption through debugging, a Java agent and decompiled class code; some extracted files also require GZIP decompression.
requirements: User-supplied ODIS plugin and DIDB data files.
Python with pycryptodome and blowfish installed.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: rust-sig-gen
resources.description: rust-sig-gen generates IDA FLAIR library signatures from compiled Rust crates for executable analysis. Its Python script obtains the top 100 crates, builds them for Linux and x86-64 Windows, and processes the outputs with sigmake, pelf and pcf.
requirements: Python packages requests and toml, a Rust compiler, and IDA Pro FLAIR tools sigmake, pelf and pcf are required.
The documented scope is the top 100 Rust crates and Linux and x86-64 Windows builds.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: tMock-Server: reconstructing Terraria server handshakes
resources.description: tMock-Server is an unfinished C++ reimplementation of the Terraria server's initial network flow. It uses socket code and packet classes to accept connections, check protocol versions, request passwords, and assign player slots; the README records packet IDs, fields, directions, and structures informed by traffic analysis.
requirements: GNU/Linux is currently required because the server relies on its socket support.
CMake 4.1 and a C++26 toolchain are specified by the build file.
Player and world information handling remain unfinished.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: 1C 7.7 Configuration Parser (MD Parser)
resources.description: 1C 7.7 Configuration Parser inspects 1C:Enterprise 7.7 1cv7.md configuration containers. Its Win32 interface displays OLE streams, decompresses ZLib data, removes the documented XOR layer and parses Main MetaData Stream into an object hierarchy.
requirements: Windows and a 1cv7.md configuration file are required.
Building uses Visual Studio or Build Tools with NMAKE.
MIT license.

resources.name: x64dbg-tenet
resources.description: x64dbg-tenet is a native x64dbg plugin that records execution steps in Tenet trace format. Commands start and stop logging or trace a specified number of steps, with an option to stop when execution leaves the current module.
requirements: x64dbg is required.
MIT license.

resources.name: VanMoof BLE: a client for S5, A5 and S6 bicycle protocols
resources.description: VanMoof BLE implements a Python client for the S5, A5 and S6 bicycle BLE protocols. It authenticates with an Ed25519 certificate, reads and writes documented topics, decodes captured messages, and exposes controls and telemetry according to each model's message format.
requirements: A VanMoof S5, A5 or S6, a BLE-capable device, Python 3.8+, and the bike certificate and private key.
Region changes, streaming telemetry and module status are listed for S5/A5 only.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Holley EFI Parser
resources.description: Holley EFI Parser decodes Holley DL and DLZ data logs and live ECU CAN messages. Its Python tools decompress DLZ with byte swapping and RLE, parse versioned DL records into pandas DataFrames, and decode CAN messages using supplied DBC files. The documentation records the proprietary 29-bit CAN identifier layout.
requirements: Python and the package dependencies are required; live CAN use additionally needs a configured Linux CAN interface.
V4 DL support is partial, and V5 files require conversion to V6 with Holley software.
The author reports DLZ decompression accuracy from nine file pairs.
MIT License.

resources.name: CAN Bus Parser
resources.description: CAN Bus Parser decodes VanMoof SA5 and later bicycle CAN captures from CSV or candump input. It reassembles multi-frame CBOR messages, maps device IDs and heartbeat frames, and provides live or saved-capture diagnostics for components such as the electronic lock and shifter.
requirements: Go 1.24 or newer.
Live capture requires Linux SocketCAN and a CAN adapter supporting 1 Mbps and 29-bit extended IDs.

resources.name: Cosmic Byte Firestorm Controller: a USB protocol client for mouse settings
resources.description: Cosmic Byte Firestorm Controller implements a Linux client for the mouse's recovered USB settings protocol. Its Python CLI sends control and interrupt transfers to configure lighting effects, per-DPI indicator colours and sensitivity levels, while PROTOCOL.md records packet structures and command sequences.
requirements: Linux and a Cosmic Byte Firestorm mouse with VID 0x04d9 and PID 0xa09f; USB access typically requires sudo.
Running from source requires Python, pyusb and PyYAML.
Device support was tested only with the named Firestorm model.
GPL-3.0 licence.

resources.name: NuVelocity Engine: reimplementing Reflexive's Velocity Engine
resources.description: NuVelocity Engine reimplements Reflexive Entertainment's Velocity Engine as a C++ and SDL3 game engine. It provides modular 2D rendering, asset and resource loading, audio playback, screen management, and a property-based object system, with decoder source included in the repository.
requirements: SDL3, SDL3_image, SDL3_mixer, SDL3_ttf, zlib, physfs, CMake, and submodules are required for the documented build.
Mozilla Public License 2.0 applies to the engine and main code.

resources.name: FreeRS42: reimplementing Ricochet Xtreme
resources.description: FreeRS42 is a C++ project to reimplement the PC game Ricochet Xtreme using the NuVelocity engine. The repository contains source for game objects, playfield behavior and screens, with a CMake build that includes the engine submodule.
requirements: Clone the repository with submodules and install the engine dependencies documented by the project.
MPL-2.0 license for the main code and engine.

resources.name: Universal GBA Pokedex
resources.description: Universal GBA Pokedex scans Game Boy Advance Pokémon ROMs to locate and display evolution, name and item tables. It searches byte signatures, scores candidate tables using text and pointer patterns, and aligns entries against known anchors instead of requiring fixed offsets.
requirements: Requires a Game Boy Advance Pokémon ROM supplied by the user.
Running from source requires Python 3.x and Tkinter.
Support for expanded Pokédex hacks such as Radical Red is experimental.
MIT licence.

resources.name: NullSec BinGaze
resources.description: NullSec BinGaze analyses ELF executables by parsing headers, listing sections and calculating entropy. It also reports NX stack, PIE, RELRO, stack-canary and RWX-segment properties through command-line modes for full analysis, section listing or security assessment.
requirements: A C++20 compiler and CMake are required to build it.
The README labels the licence NullSec Proprietary; the file list contains no licence file.

resources.name: Centerpiece Projects: decoding Finalmouse Centerpiece USB control
resources.description: Centerpiece Projects documents observed USB control messages for the Finalmouse Centerpiece keyboard and implements scripts around them. Its notes describe HID framing and message types for uploads, status, slot switching and preview chunks; PowerShell and Python helpers expose device operations.
requirements: A connected Finalmouse Centerpiece, Windows 10 or later, PowerShell and Python for the public scripts.
The vendor-specific WinUSB bulk interface remains under investigation, and the notes are not a complete protocol specification.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Facebook BitMap Codec
resources.description: Facebook BitMap Codec encodes and decodes Facebook web API parameter values using the project's reverse-engineered bitmap, run-length and custom Base64 scheme. Its Python module exposes a FacebookCodec class for converting ID lists to encoded strings and back across parameters including __dyn and __csr.
requirements: Python 3.8+ and the FCodec.py module are required.
The author claims lossless conversion and compatibility with the listed bitmap parameters.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: pdbinspector
resources.description: pdbinspector analyzes Microsoft PDB files to list structures, classes, enums, functions, public symbols and exports. It demangles MSVC C++ names, decodes MSVC string literals and emits text, JSON or tab-separated reports through a CLI; a WebAssembly version runs online.
requirements: A Microsoft PDB file is required as input.
Building from source requires Rust; the manifest specifies Rust 1.75 or later.
MIT License.

resources.name: Assassin's Creed III online service docs
resources.description: Assassin's Creed III online service docs record method IDs and request and response fields for the PC game's online services. The files cover RMC services such as online saves and account management, alongside notes on P2P Duplicated Objects over PRUDP.
requirements: Scope is Assassin's Creed III PC online services.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: AOL 7.0 Retro Server: reconstructing the P3 server session
resources.description: AOL 7.0 Retro Server implements local Python servers for the 2001 AOL 7.0 client. It reconstructs the proprietary P3 login and security exchange, the handoff between login and BOS servers, and post-login data used to display the welcome screen and buddy list.
requirements: Python 3.x and an installed English or German AOL 7.0 client on a VM or older machine are required.
Interactive chat rooms, email simulation and keyword navigation remain on the roadmap.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: VG Reverse Engineering
resources.description: VG Reverse Engineering decodes Vainglory: Community Edition replay files into recorded player names, heroes, K/D/A, items, gold and scoreboard counters. Its offline tools also export JSON and CSV, maintain a SQLite catalog and document VGR record and event interpretation. Output records provenance and leaves unsupported values unresolved.
requirements: Python 3.12 or newer for the offline decoder; the complete regression suite also requires Node.js 18 or newer.
A user's own .0.vgr recording and numbered sibling files are needed for decoding a match.
The source says recordings lack a client build identifier and currently cannot enter its definitive-analysis subset.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: 8086 Register Command Debugger
resources.description: 8086 Register Command Debugger is an MS-DOS machine-code inspection tool written in 8086 assembly. It loads a program into a 64 KB segment, decodes 8086 instructions and lets users inspect or edit memory and registers while stepping through real CPU instructions using the Trap Flag.
requirements: MS-DOS or a compatible environment such as DOSBox is needed to run the executable.
The program uses a 64 KB memory segment and original 8086 instructions.
MIT license.

resources.name: AC4 docs
resources.description: AC4 docs records online service interfaces for the PC version of Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag. Its RMC documents list method IDs and request and response types, while the repository also contains HTTP API specifications for service revival work.
requirements: Scope is the PC online services of Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: DevLens Ultra
resources.description: DevLens Ultra is a Chrome extension for inspecting and extracting website component structure. It analyzes selected DOM elements, computed styles and framework state such as React Fiber props, then generates React JSX and Tailwind classes. An optional AI step refines selected snippets through a configured provider.
requirements: Chrome with extension Developer Mode to load the unpacked extension.
AI refinement requires a configured provider API key and base URL.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: FAAC E145 Gate Connect: reconstructing EasyBoard gate commands
resources.description: FAAC E145 Gate Connect implements local control of an FAAC E145 gate through serial commands reconstructed from EasyBoard software traffic. The documentation lists POLL, OPEN, CLOSE and STOP byte sequences and describes their framing and checksum. The Python gateway adds position monitoring plus web, REST and MQTT interfaces.
requirements: An FAAC E145 controller connected by serial or USB, Python 3.8+ and the documented dependencies.
MIT.

resources.name: stagg-net: investigating the Fellow Stagg EKG kettle UART
resources.description: stagg-net investigates the Fellow Stagg EKG kettle's internal UART interface and documents its connector, serial settings, observed heartbeat packet, and startup message. The repository includes a logic capture, decoder source, probing scripts, and ESPHome configuration for an ESP32-C6 connection.
requirements: Fellow Stagg EKG kettle hardware and a 3.3 V serial connection are needed for the described investigation.
The author has observed status traffic but reports that the UART interface does not respond to the BLE packets tried.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Malware Analysis & CTI Reports
resources.description: Malware Analysis & CTI Reports collects ten PDF investigations of malware, security tools and binaries with disputed detections. The author describes static inspection with Detect It Easy, strings and imports, followed by manual disassembly or decompilation in Ghidra or radare2.
requirements: Reports are PDF files; the repository does not include live malware samples.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: advantage
resources.description: advantage is a Windows research tool for inspecting Lenovo Vantage and add-in RPC commands. It injects a stub into a Lenovo-signed process, supplies an RPC JSON payload from a local server, and returns the command response through a CLI or web interface; the repository also contains Frida contract and request dump scripts.
requirements: A Windows Lenovo Vantage process is required for the documented RPC path.
Go 1.25 or newer and donut are required by the documented build procedure.
Apache-2.0 license.

resources.name: Chip-8 Emulator and c8-disassembler
resources.description: The c8-disassembler in Chip-8 Emulator translates CHIP-8 ROM opcodes into assembly instructions. Its source and sample Pong ROM listing show the supported output; the repository also contains a companion emulator whose SDL2 display is marked as work in progress.
requirements: CMake 3.9 or newer is required to build the disassembler; the emulator also requires SDL2.
Super Chip-48 instructions are listed as unsupported.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: eRepublik API Documentation
resources.description: eRepublik API Documentation maps endpoints observed in the browser-based strategy game's web client. Its reference pages cover authentication cookies and requests for travel, battles, economy, social features and other game functions, with HTTP methods and example parameters.
requirements: Most documented endpoints require authentication.
The source warns that undocumented endpoints may change or stop working.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Garmin Strength Workout API
resources.description: Garmin Strength Workout API documents payloads for creating strength workouts through Garmin Connect's undocumented API. Its reference describes repeat groups, exercise and rest steps, conditions, weights and exercise identifiers, with JSON examples plus a small builder and validator.
requirements: Garmin Connect OAuth tokens are required to call the workout endpoint.
The source warns that the undocumented API may change.
MIT License.

resources.name: netdumper
resources.description: netdumper extracts loaded .NET assemblies from Windows processes through the CLR Data Access Component. It enumerates AppDomains and assemblies, recovers JIT method IL, converts memory layouts to PE files, and repairs damaged PE headers or metadata streams for subsequent inspection.
requirements: Windows, Rust nightly, and the same architecture as the target process are required.
Administrator privileges may be required for some processes.
MIT License.

resources.name: TOZO Control: a Linux earbuds client built from the TOZO BLE protocol
resources.description: TOZO Control provides a Linux GTK4 client for TOZO earbuds using a BLE GATT protocol recovered from the vendor's Android app. It sends commands to characteristic B611, receives notifications on B612, and documents GET and SET packet layouts and parameter IDs. The author reports testing the T10 model for battery, game mode, equalizer and balance controls.
requirements: Linux with GTK4, libadwaita, BlueZ and the Python bleak package; a compatible TOZO BLE earbud is needed.
Only TOZO T10 is reported as tested; command support varies by model.
MIT License.

resources.name: BMS RS485 Service Suite: reconstructing a battery-service bus protocol
resources.description: BMS RS485 Service Suite documents an observed ASCII RS485 protocol for battery-management services and implements frame building and decoding in Node-RED. The specification covers framing, length and checksum fields, request and response rules and decoded service IDs; the wider suite connects JK and DALY BLE data to MQTT and dashboards.
requirements: A Raspberry Pi and Node-RED are the documented service environment; BLE gateways use MQTT and optional Python dependencies.
The specification records observed and currently decoded RS485 services; some write acknowledgements are handled generically.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: BGI Converter TGA
resources.description: BGI Converter TGA analyzes BGI-Ethornell game image files and converts custom RGB or RGBA layouts and BMP images into 32-bit TGA. Its C++17 utility detects formats from headers, reports dimensions and offsets, and supports single-file or batch conversion.
requirements: Requires a C++17 compiler with std::filesystem support.
Inputs are the documented BMP 24-bit, BMP 32-bit, BGI custom RGBA or BGI custom RGB layouts.
MIT license.

resources.name: Valkyrie
resources.description: Valkyrie analyzes suspect binaries through static inspection and Docker-based execution. Its documented pipeline examines PE headers, entropy and packing, then captures system calls, file activity and PCAP traffic for reports and threat-intelligence output.
requirements: Python 3.9+ is required; dynamic analysis requires Docker Desktop or Docker Engine.
Optional API keys enable VirusTotal and OpenAI integrations.
MIT License.

resources.name: PE Disassembler
resources.description: PE Disassembler is a WPF application that extracts the .text section of 32-bit Windows PE executables and displays decoded x86 instructions. It checks MZ and PE signatures, handles a limited set of movement, arithmetic and control-flow opcodes, and can save the listing as text.
requirements: Windows with .NET Framework 4.7.2+ or .NET 5/6/7/8 with WPF support; Visual Studio 2019/2022 to build.
Only 32-bit x86 PE files and implemented opcodes are supported; output uses raw file offsets without relocation handling.
MIT License.

resources.name: SIC/XE Disassembler and Linking Loader
resources.description: SIC/XE Disassembler and Linking Loader converts SIC/XE object code into assembly listings and reconstructed symbols. Its first pass identifies instruction boundaries and addressing modes; its second emits assembly, while a separate loader resolves external symbols and applies relocation records.
requirements: A C++17 compiler is required.
Character-literal reconstruction is limited, and the loader assumes well-formed object files.
MIT license.

resources.name: Xenus DT1 Decompiler
resources.description: Xenus DT1 Decompiler extracts DT1 and DT2 texture caches from Xenus 2: White Gold and Boiling Point: Road to Hell; its current decoder has not been tested with The Precursors. Its C# decoder reimplements behavior recovered from VELoader.dll, handles zlib and UCL NRV2E streams, and exports DDS or converted image formats.
requirements: The release targets 64-bit Windows; building requires .NET SDK 8.0 or later.
The Precursors has not been checked with the decoder used since version 3.0; method 7's additional encryption is unsupported.
MIT license.

resources.name: Lutron Protocols
resources.description: Lutron Protocols researches CCA radio packets, CCX Thread and CoAP messages, the LEAP processor API and IPL Designer integration frames for Lutron lighting systems. Its documentation covers device behavior and firmware, while TypeScript tools capture and decode traffic and parse Designer project files.
requirements: Packet-capture hardware uses an STM32H723 Nucleo with CC1101 and nRF52840 radios.
LEAP tools require mutual TLS certificates.
Native Vive pairing and a long-running LEAP connection watchdog remain future work.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: SteelSeries Overlay Hook: mapping and hooking the GameOverlay swapchain
resources.description: SteelSeries Overlay Hook documents IDA analysis of SteelSeriesGameOverlay.dll’s window, object layout and Direct3D 11 swapchain, then uses recovered offsets in a C++ DLL hook. Its injector and hook render Dear ImGui content through the existing GameOverlay window by intercepting Present and ResizeBuffers.
requirements: Windows, Visual Studio 2022 with the v143 C++ toolset, and a Windows 10 SDK are required to build.
The hook relies on fixed internal offsets; compatibility with other SteelSeries versions is not established.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Sandwitcher
resources.description: Sandwitcher instruments Java and Kotlin method calls in Android apps by replacing ART method entry points with a trampoline through Pine and LSPlant. Its AAR exposes callbacks before and after the original call to inspect or change arguments and results and inspect thrown exceptions; it also includes a demo application.
requirements: Android and the AAR integration are required; building from source needs JDK 17 and Android SDK 35.
The README lists Android 5.0 through 15 compatibility.
Apache License 2.0.

resources.name: Bin X-ray
resources.description: Bin X-ray visualizes byte patterns in unknown files and firmware blobs through a 256×256 byte-pair matrix and a 3D byte-trigram plot. A sliding window, ribbon overview, transition-offset search and hex view let analysts move from a pattern to its bytes in the file.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11; building requires Visual Studio 2022, Windows SDK 10.0 or newer, and Python 3 for the version helper.
Bookmarks, entropy strips, comparison mode and structured decoders are roadmap items.
MIT license.

resources.name: Malware Deobfuscator
resources.description: Malware Deobfuscator analyzes obfuscated malware scripts and generates code, behavior and indicator reports. A deterministic pass extracts indicators with regexes and maps keyword signatures to MITRE ATT&CK; an OpenAI or Ollama model supplies deobfuscated code and execution-flow explanations. The CLI handles individual files or directories and can emit JSON.
requirements: Python 3.9 or later is specified in the package metadata.
Full analysis requires an OpenAI API key or a configured Ollama model; IOC extraction works without one.
The included samples are described as defanged educational examples.
MIT license.

resources.name: PIC microcontrollers disassembler
resources.description: PIC microcontrollers disassembler converts Intel HEX dumps for MidRange and Enhanced MidRange PIC12/PIC16 devices into disassembly listings, HI-TECH PICC assembly files, or both. Processor descriptions and instruction definitions are supplied as JSON configuration files.
requirements: An Intel HEX dump and the matching PIC12/PIC16 processor selection are required.
Support is stated for MidRange and Enhanced MidRange PIC12/PIC16 devices.
MIT.

resources.name: flashkit
resources.description: flashkit is a Python toolkit for examining Adobe Flash SWF files and AVM2 bytecode. It parses and rebuilds SWF and ABC structures, disassembles instructions, constructs call and reference indexes, and decompiles classes or methods to ActionScript 3 through a control-flow pipeline.
requirements: Python 3.10 or later.
SWF or AVM2 bytecode input for analysis.
Dead-code detection is heuristic because ActionScript 3 dynamic dispatch cannot be fully ruled out.
MIT License.

resources.name: Petkit Local: reconstructing feeder cloud and fountain BLE controls
resources.description: Petkit Local replaces selected Petkit D4 feeder cloud exchanges with a local Home Assistant server and relays Eversweet Max 2 CTW3 fountain messages over BLE. The integration implements device registration, heartbeats, schedules, events and commands based on observed device communication.
requirements: Home Assistant 2024.1 or newer, a D4-family feeder, port 80 and local DNS or IP redirection are required.
CTW3 fountain support requires a D4 feeder already running the integration.
The documented tested firmware versions are D4 1.267 and CTW3 1.11.
MIT licence.

resources.name: AppThreat wasm-tools
resources.description: wasm-tools is a pure-Python parser and disassembler for WebAssembly core modules and Component Model binaries. It reports sections, decoded instructions, strings with memory provenance, imports, exports and static call graphs, then adds heuristic capability and risk findings in JSON.
requirements: Python 3.10 or later is specified in pyproject.toml.
Text-format .wat parsing and specification validation are excluded.
MIT license; the author raises uncertainty about third-party specification text in the AI-assisted code provenance.

resources.name: dos-mcp
resources.description: dos-mcp connects AI agents to DOS programs running in js-dos for interactive reverse engineering. Its MCP tools send keyboard and mouse input, capture frames, exchange files with the guest and read or search emulated memory; the documentation shows a save-format comparison workflow using Ultima Underworld.
requirements: Node.js 22.13 or newer is required; Puppeteer installs a browser dependency.
A DOS program or bundle is needed as input.
Save-state snapshot and restore are missing; breakpoints and stepping are only proposed.
MIT License.

resources.name: premium5
resources.description: premium5 emulates the Volkswagen Premium 5 car radio at the register and signal level so its original firmware can run without patches. It models the NEC microcontroller, LCD controller, EEPROM and selected vehicle interfaces, with live disassembly, memory inspection and execution controls for firmware research.
requirements: A Premium 5 firmware binary is required.
PyPy and a modern CPU with strong single-threaded performance are needed to emulate the original 4.19 MHz speed.
Audio output and the tape deck are not emulated.
BSD-3-Clause.

resources.name: IPI STAY FLY Driver: reconstructing mouse configuration over HID
resources.description: IPI STAY FLY Driver reconstructs mouse configuration in a Windows app using reverse-engineered 16-byte HID frames. It exposes DPI, polling, button and sensor settings, documents a frame checksum, and includes a WebHID capture extension plus protocol notes for ATK FIERCE X.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, WebView2 and an IPI STAY FLY mouse are required for device control.
Building from source requires Node.js 20 or later, Rust and Visual Studio Build Tools 2022.
Non-mouse button actions, including keyboard keys and macros, are not yet exposed.
MIT license.

resources.name: Kaiju
resources.description: Kaiju is a Rust reverse-engineering framework with a headless CLI for binary loading and analysis. Its current crates parse selected ELF, PE and Mach-O metadata, extract strings, decode a limited x86-64 instruction subset and inspect saved network evidence.
requirements: Rust 1.76+ is specified by the workspace.
ELF, PE, Mach-O and x86-64 support is limited to the documented parser and decoder subsets.
Apache-2.0.

resources.name: x64dbg MCP
resources.description: x64dbg MCP gives agents debugger control over Windows binaries through a native x64dbg plugin and a C# stdio MCP server. The plugin serves local HTTP requests to x64dbg's bridge API, while MCP tools expose disassembly, memory and register access, modules, execution control, and breakpoints.
requirements: Windows, Visual Studio 2022, CMake 3.20 or newer, .NET 10 SDK, and a built x64dbg checkout.
The plugin's HTTP endpoint binds to localhost and grants control over the debugged process.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: Metroid Dread: a hand decompilation in progress
resources.description: DreadComp is an in-progress hand decompilation of Metroid Dread that recreates game source code in C++. The repository includes initial source files, build tooling and symbol data; building requires assets and the version 2.1.0 executable from the user's own game copy.
requirements: An owned copy of Metroid Dread and its original 2.1.0 main NSO executable are required.
Windows users are directed to use WSL; installation lists Python, Ninja, CMake, ccache, xdelta3, Clang and a Rust toolchain.
The decompilation is a work in progress.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Soundcore D3200: reconstructing BLE recording transfer and decryption
resources.description: A Soundcore D3200 investigation reconstructs the BLE exchange used to list and transfer encrypted recordings. Its Python client performs a P-256 ECDH handshake, derives session and file keys, decrypts AES-256-CTR Opus packets and writes an Ogg/Opus file.
requirements: Python 3.12 or newer, a Bluetooth adapter and an available D3200 recorder are required.
The recorder must be disconnected from the Soundcore app before connecting.
A real-recording regression test requires the user's own capture fixtures.
GPL-3.0-or-later licence.

resources.name: K1 Pro OpenDeck Suite: a Linux driver for the Stream Dock K1 Pro
resources.description: K1 Pro OpenDeck Suite includes a Linux OpenDeck driver for the HOTSPOTEK/Mirabox Stream Dock K1 Pro based on its reverse-engineered USB/HID CRT protocol. The driver handles connection and keepalive messages, 64×64 JPEG key displays, RGB ring controls, and three knob inputs. Four accompanying plugins add generic OpenDeck functions.
requirements: OpenDeck, Linux, and a Stream Dock K1 Pro with USB ID 5548:1025 and protocol v3 are required for the driver.
Building requires Rust 1.87 or later with the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu target, plus just and zip.
The driver README says this fork had not been compiled or tested on hardware before delivery.
GPLv3 license; the vendored mirajazz dependency retains MPL-2.0.

resources.name: open-picpak: reconstructing the PicPak frame's BLE protocol and device behavior
resources.description: open-picpak documents the PicPak 4.2-inch e-ink frame's stock firmware behavior, BLE GATT protocol, and image conversion pipeline. The author reports deriving byte-level findings from the stock ESP-IDF image and a device client, then using those findings in custom ESP-IDF firmware, host tools, and a self-hosted backend.
requirements: A PicPak e-ink frame is needed for device use and hardware checks.
Firmware and backend development remain in progress; the web-usb component is not public.
MPL-2.0 license.

resources.name: iDotMatrix: Home Assistant control through a reconstructed BLE protocol
resources.description: iDotMatrix Home Assistant integration controls the HXS-002 / NL-XSD-32 LED panel over a BLE protocol derived from analysis of the vendor Android app. Its vendored protocol module and hardware-capture tests support power, brightness, clock controls and chunked 32×32 image uploads with CRC32.
requirements: Home Assistant with a Bluetooth adapter or nearby ESPHome/Shelly Bluetooth proxy is required.
The panel accepts only one BLE connection at a time.
Some protocol modes, including carousel/GIF storage and rhythm/spectrum, are not exposed as Home Assistant entities.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Substack API Reference (Unofficial)
resources.description: Substack API Reference documents the web app's undocumented JSON API using curl probes and captured browser requests. It records read and write endpoints, authentication and request bodies, and supplies an OpenAPI 3.1 specification with curl and TypeScript examples. The author reports 129 verified endpoints from 14 capture rounds.
requirements: A Substack session cookie is needed for authenticated endpoints.
The internal API can change; entries distinguish author-tested, reported, inferred, dead and gated endpoints.
MIT License.

resources.name: Zygisk - Frida Gadget
resources.description: Zygisk - Frida Gadget loads Frida Gadget into selected Android app processes for runtime instrumentation. A configuration file selects packages, process names, ABIs, and profiles; deployment scripts place Gadget and its configuration in the app's native library directory before the Zygisk loader starts it.
requirements: Magisk 27001 or Kitsune Magisk with Zygisk enabled is required.
The documented ABIs are arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a; Gadget files must match the target ABI, and non-default profiles need matching configuration files.
No licence file is present in the repository.

resources.name: web-crawler ReverseAgent
resources.description: web-crawler includes ReverseAgent for investigating website JavaScript and request signing. It hooks fetch, XHR, cookies, crypto.subtle and webpack activity in a browser, captures traffic, separates webpack modules and uses an LLM to reimplement a discovered signature algorithm in Python.
requirements: Python 3.10 or newer.
ReverseAgent uses CamoufoxFetcher and a compatible LLM service; optional browser dependencies are required for that path.
MIT license.

resources.name: hyperscan-homebrew
resources.description: hyperscan-homebrew documents Mattel HyperScan hardware behavior for homebrew and emulation work. Its notes cover SPG290 PPU registers, RFID reader signaling, controller I²C behavior, SPU audio and S+Core 7 compiler failures, drawing on MAME experiments and hardware captures where available.
requirements: The documented work concerns Mattel HyperScan and its Sunplus S+Core 7/SPG290 hardware.
The notes use MAME as the working reference platform; hardware captures were available for some comparisons.
MIT license.

resources.name: Dell ControlVault 2 fingerprint on Linux: adapting a driver for BCM5880
resources.description: Dell ControlVault 2 fingerprint on Linux adapts a locally obtained Broadcom driver to the older BCM5880 fingerprint reader through five signature-matched byte patches. The accompanying investigation maps the device’s USB endpoints, command header and driver checks. The author reports working capture, while enrollment and matching remain unreliable or unconfirmed.
requirements: A Dell ControlVault 2 / Broadcom BCM5880 device with USB ID 0a5c:5834, Linux x86_64 and TOD-enabled libfprint.
The proprietary stock driver must be obtained locally from Canonical’s OEM repository.
The author reports enrollment commit failures on many units and unconfirmed verification with the included patches.
MIT license applies to the repository’s original scripts, udev rule and documentation.

resources.name: epson-l3110-driver: investigating the printer's USB and ESC/P-R exchanges
resources.description: epson-l3110-driver investigates the Epson L3110's USB printing exchanges while developing a Linux driver in C. Its notes use captured print-job traffic to identify the IEEE 1284 device ID, EJL session setup and ESC/P-R command framing. USB communication is still in progress, and the driver cannot yet print pages.
requirements: An Epson L3110 printer and Linux are needed; the current Makefile requires libusb-1.0 and libcups development files.
Printing, image processing and the CUPS filter and backend are pending.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: MS5 WiFi Microscope: reconstructing the camera's UDP video protocol
resources.description: MS5 WiFi Microscope reconstructs the MS5 camera's UDP command and video protocol and supplies a Python client that serves its reassembled JPEG stream as MJPEG. The documentation specifies command headers, the OpenVideo port handshake, chunk layout and resolution queries; the author reports 1280×720 streaming at roughly 25–30 fps on MS5 hardware.
requirements: Python 3.7 or newer and a computer connected to the microscope's Wi-Fi access point.
Compatibility is reported for the MS5; related i4season devices are suggested but unconfirmed.
MIT license.

resources.name: lux-lat-long-log: reconstructing LUMIX S5 BLE GPS communication
resources.description: lux-lat-long-log reconstructs the Panasonic LUMIX S5 Bluetooth LE GPS exchange in an ESP32 camera client. The project documents GATT identifiers, session ordering and GPS/time packets from Android HCI captures, then uses a GNSS module to send positions without the phone app.
requirements: Requires an ESP32 and SIM868 GNSS module for the documented hardware build.
Builds with PlatformIO; the documented camera implementation targets the LUMIX S5.
The author reports successful hardware and photo EXIF checks for the S5.
MIT licence.

resources.name: MTG Arena Collection Export: reconstructing the Frontdoor collection request
resources.description: MTG Arena Collection Export reconstructs the Frontdoor request needed to export owned cards from Magic: The Gathering Arena. The Python client uses an account refresh token, opens a TLS Frontdoor socket, authenticates with the 2026 version 4 frame and protobuf command envelope, and requests Card_GetAllCards. A separate protocol document records the recovered wire format.
requirements: Requires Python 3.8 or newer and a captured refresh token from the user's own Arena account.
Requires a captured doorbell response or a Frontdoor URI; the source says Arena should be closed during export.
MIT licence.

resources.name: Magene L308: reconstructing a smart taillight's BLE control protocol
resources.description: Magene L308 interop tools reconstruct the smart taillight's BLE control protocol and light_mode.bin pattern format. A protocol specification records GATT characteristics, command frames and upload sequences; browser, Python and Garmin clients use those findings to control settings and patterns directly.
requirements: A Magene L308 light is required; the Python CLI uses bleak.
The web client requires Chrome or Edge with Web Bluetooth in an HTTPS or localhost context.
Pattern uploads replace the whole on-device store, which has no read-back; keep exported .bin backups.
Code is MIT licensed; the protocol specification is CC-BY-4.0 licensed.

resources.name: Void Client: rebuilding the Starblast.io client
resources.description: Void Client is an unfinished JavaScript rewrite of the Starblast.io browser game client based on study of its network protocol. Its current Node.js and browser components provide game-mode selection, server discovery, local WebSocket communication, and parsing and JSON export of some received packets.
requirements: Node.js and the package.json dependencies are required.
The client is a work in progress; current functionality covers menus, network helpers, and basic packet parsing.
The package.json declares an ISC license; the repository has no separate license file.

resources.name: xbloom-ble: a client for the xBloom Studio BLE protocol
resources.description: xbloom-ble implements a Python client for the xBloom Studio coffee machine's recovered Bluetooth LE protocol. The author documents capturing app traffic and comparing GATT command frames; the CLI and terminal UI load recipes, program dial presets, optionally start brewing and display live scale telemetry.
requirements: An xBloom Studio machine and Bluetooth LE access are required; the phone app must disconnect before writes because the machine accepts one BLE link.
Python 3.10 or newer, with bleak and PyYAML; Linux also requires BlueZ.
The author tested only one machine running firmware V12.0D.500.
Remote start dispenses near-boiling water and requires the machine to be physically ready.
MIT licence.

resources.name: ak820: reconstructing AJAZZ AK820 Pro HID control on macOS
resources.description: ak820 implements macOS control of the AJAZZ AK820 Pro keyboard through its vendor HID feature-report protocol. The Python CLI sets the clock, RGB lighting, and sleep timer over USB; accompanying notes describe Windows-driver analysis, packet framing, transaction handshakes, and the unresolved key-remapping commands.
requirements: macOS, Python 3.11+, and an AJAZZ AK820 Pro connected with a USB-C data cable are required.
The Python package depends on hidapi.
LCD image upload on macOS and key remapping are unsupported.
MIT license.

resources.name: GRB Modding Knowledgebase
resources.description: GRB Modding Knowledgebase documents Ghost Recon: Breakpoint’s Anvil .forge archives, nested .data resources and asset replacement workflow. Its Python inspectors examine MotionCloth files, list resource types, compare forge indexes and diff gameplay database records to explore field layouts.
requirements: Inspection requires Ghost Recon: Breakpoint game data; the Data Inspector uses the game’s DLL for Oodle decompression.
The project describes itself as a living research project with open questions.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: WeChat: recovering SQLCipher keys through CommonCrypto hooks
resources.description: An investigation of WeChat 4.1.10 for macOS reports recovering per-database SQLCipher keys by breaking on CommonCrypto encryption calls in LLDB. It compares that approach with memory scanning and sqlite3_key breakpoints, and describes an offline check against a decrypted SQLite page.
requirements: WeChat 4.1.10 on Apple Silicon macOS, with LLDB and access to the user's own app data.
The author reports testing on one machine running macOS 26.5.1.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: GameTrak Liberation: a client for the controller's HID protocol
resources.description: GameTrak Liberation implements a client for the GameTrak controller's reverse-engineered USB HID behavior. It sends the initialization and rolling-key keepalive messages needed for sustained reports, then exposes six-axis data through stdout, OSC, MIDI or WebSockets. Protocol notes, report captures and Processing and p5.js examples accompany the Python tools.
requirements: A GameTrak controller is required for live capture; offline playback accepts recorded JSONL reports.
The author tested a GameTrak V2.0 unit on macOS 15.6 with Python 3.10 and 3.14.
The footswitch was unavailable for testing and is unsupported.
MIT license.

resources.name: Cooper Hunter AC: UART and infrared protocol investigation
resources.description: Cooper Hunter AC documents the COM1 UART and infrared control messages of CH-IF140RK and CH-IF140RK2 units with a Gree GRZQ3-R V1 board. The author inferred UART status fields by comparing packets while operating the infrared remote. The resulting ESPHome design receives UART status and sends control through an infrared signal path.
requirements: Cooper Hunter CH-IF140RK or CH-IF140RK2 with the documented Gree GRZQ3-R V1 board, plus an ESP32 running ESPHome for the described setup.
The final wiring uses UART receive only; control uses infrared signal injection.
Some protocol fields are marked tentative in PROTOCOL.md.
MIT license.

resources.name: Локальный аудиостриминг на Яндекс.Станцию
resources.description: Local audio streaming on Yandex Station is a technical guide to the device’s Glagol WebSocket control channel and its HTTP audio-stream behavior. It documents radio_play, token acquisition, message formats and MP3 CBR stream requirements, including an exact Content-Length.
requirements: A Yandex Station on the local network and an account Session_id to obtain a short-lived Glagol token.
An HTTP server serving MP3 CBR with an exact Content-Length.
The author tested a first-generation Yandex Station; other Quasar models were not tested.
Documentation text is CC BY 4.0; code snippets are MIT.

resources.name: psp-media-slopkit
resources.description: psp-media-slopkit analyses PSP XMB ICON1.PMF and SND0.AT3 files using format findings derived from retail game samples. Its Python CLI checks media against documented XMB limits, converts video and audio into icon media, and inserts the results into a homebrew EBOOT.PBP. FINDINGS.md records PSMF container fields, H.264 constraints and AT3 playback behaviour.
requirements: Python 3.8 or newer; video conversion requires ffmpeg and ffprobe with libx264.
SND0.AT3 creation requires atracdenc; ATRAC3+ output requires Sony's at3tool.exe.
PBP repacking requires an existing homebrew EBOOT.PBP.
The author reports hardware checks of generated ICON1.PMF and SND0.AT3 media.
MIT license.

resources.name: Siriously: recovering macOS Writing Tools entry points
resources.description: Siriously investigates how macOS 27 changed access to Writing Tools and restores its popover through a Services client. The author used Objective-C runtime introspection and behavioral tracing to identify private WritingToolsUI classes, then passes selected text to the popover and writes accepted results back through Accessibility APIs. The findings concern one macOS build.
requirements: A Mac with Apple Intelligence and the new Siri enabled is required.
The author reports operation on macOS 27.0 build 26A5368g on arm64.
Accessibility permission is required to read selections and write results back.
Private framework behavior can change with OS updates.
MIT license.

resources.name: sqlce
resources.description: sqlce reads SQL Server Compact .sdf database files using a cross-platform C++ parser informed by analysis of decompiled SQL CE components. Python and WebAssembly bindings expose table names, schemas and rows, including files encrypted with a supplied password.
requirements: An existing .sdf file is required; encrypted files need a password.
The comparison test suite requires Windows with SQL Server Compact 4.0 installed.
MIT license.

resources.name: DualRip
resources.description: DualRip extracts Nintendo DS sound effects and music from SDAT archives and Nintendo 3DS audio from CSAR archives, including ROM inputs. It parses sequence, wave and stream formats, emulates the consoles' sound drivers for rendering and exports WAV files with loop points through CLI and GUI frontends.
requirements: Python 3.10+ with NumPy, ndspy and pyctr is required; the GUI additionally uses PySide6 and sounddevice.
Encrypted 3DS ROMs require the user's boot9.bin dump; no game data is included.
MIT License.

resources.name: aw5d-linux: driving an iBUYPOWER cooler LCD from USB-HID research
resources.description: aw5d-linux drives the round LCD on an iBUYPOWER AW5/AW5D cooler from Linux using a 64-byte USB-HID output report. Its research notes document report ID 0x10 and byte positions for CPU usage, clock, temperature and gauge styling. The author reports a working display on one 3402:0407 unit; other device variants remain unconfirmed.
requirements: Linux, Python 3.8+ and an iBUYPOWER AW5/AW5D cooler with USB access.
Only the 3402:0407 variant is confirmed; custom image and GIF display modes are outside the current scope.
MIT License.

resources.name: Mirrorframe
resources.description: Mirrorframe captures webpages with Playwright and reconstructs their observed layout and behavior as a self-contained React app. It records computed styles, assets, motion and selected interaction states, then compares rendered nodes and replayed states against the original with image diffs.
requirements: Node.js 18 or later and Playwright Chromium are required.
The 0.x CLI, genome schema and report format may change.
Live Canvas, WebGL and WebGPU drawing programs are not reconstructed; Canvas output is a captured still.
MIT License.

resources.name: adb-mcp
resources.description: adb-mcp gives agents structured Android Debug Bridge tools for investigating app behavior on a device. It can launch packages, inspect the UI hierarchy, capture logcat records and screenshots, retrieve files, and set up port forwarding. Its documentation shows a command sequence for investigating an in-app action through UI interaction and logs.
requirements: Python 3.10 or newer, Android platform-tools adb, and an MCP client.
An Android device or emulator is needed for device operations.
The general run_shell tool is disabled unless explicitly enabled.
MIT license.

resources.name: Hacking the Xbox — 日本語訳
resources.description: Hacking the Xbox — 日本語訳 publishes a Japanese translation of a book on Xbox reverse engineering. The repository includes translated introductory material and chapters 1–6 with figures; later chapters and appendices remain pending.
requirements: Japanese reading ability.
Chapters 7–13 and appendices A–F are not started; earlier sections remain under review.
Book-derived text, images and translations: CC BY-NC-SA 1.0; scripts and site configuration: MIT.

resources.name: inkterop
resources.description: inkterop converts native handwriting files from note apps and e-ink devices through a documented intermediate representation. It reads stroke data including pressure and tilt where present, implements readers for formats such as GoodNotes and Notability, and publishes format investigation notes and conversion fidelity modes.
requirements: Python 3.12 or later and uv for the documented setup.
Native note files in a supported input format.
Several formats are read-only or partial; GoodNotes reads ink and color, while Nebo's BINK ink codec remains under investigation.
MIT License for code; CC BY 4.0 for documentation.

resources.name: MyJBxHeadsetControl: JBL Quantum 950 controls over USB HID
resources.description: MyJBxHeadsetControl provides Stream Deck controls for the JBL Quantum 950 Wireless headset through its USB dongle's reverse-engineered HID exchange. It receives status packets for battery and sound modes, sends feature reports for settings, and uses the user's QuantumENGINE DLL to calculate EQ coefficients.
requirements: JBL Quantum 950 Wireless and its 2.4 GHz USB dongle; Stream Deck software 7.1 or newer.
Windows 10 or 11; the author states macOS is untested.
EQ actions require a local QuantumENGINE installation and its DLL.
MIT license.

resources.name: SPRD Flash Tool
resources.description: SPRD Flash Tool implements the SPRD/UNISOC PAC download protocol in Rust for RDA8910 and UIS8910 devices. Its analysis functions read partitions or whole flash through READ_FLASH and infer a proposed BMAConfig layout from U-Boot, LuatOS and filesystem regions; the author reports byte comparisons on an Air724UG.
requirements: Rust 1.85 or newer and a compatible SPRD/UNISOC device; PAC input supplies the download stages for device reads.
The proposed layout uses generic content-type names because flash data does not store partition roles.
The author reports hardware checks on an Air724UG RDA8910.
MIT license.

resources.name: OpenPigeon: reconstructing GamePigeon iMessage game messages
resources.description: OpenPigeon is a TypeScript codec for reading GamePigeon iMessage game state and encoding caller-supplied moves for eleven turn-based games. Its protocol documentation describes balloon identity, encrypted move URLs, the length-seeded cipher and the state envelope; captured-message vectors support codec tests.
requirements: Node.js 22 or newer.
Sending through Linq or Photon requires an account and host; Linq webhooks require a public endpoint.
The SDK handles turn-based payloads; live Play Now mode and move selection are outside its scope.
MIT license.

resources.name: zlt: MTN ZLT T10D MAX router API reconstruction
resources.description: zlt reconstructs the LAN JSON API of the MTN ZLT T10D MAX router from its served JavaScript and observed responses. Its Python client handles reqproc requests, login and CSRF behavior, while a CLI and local dashboard expose signal, network mode, SMS and USSD operations. The protocol document identifies firmware-specific fields and porting limits.
requirements: An MTN ZLT T10D MAX router on the LAN for the documented device behavior.
Python 3.11 or newer; authenticated operations require the router administrator password.
The author reports live checks against firmware CPE_NV8645_230A_E_QX_CAN-P42U17-20250703; other firmware may differ.
MIT license.

resources.name: claude-rc-api: reconstructing Claude Code Remote Control endpoints
resources.description: claude-rc-api reconstructs the private HTTP interface used to control local Claude Code sessions from claude.ai/code. Its reference derives session endpoints, OAuth authentication, event envelopes, and streaming behavior from the CLI binary; a Python library and CLI use that interface to observe and steer sessions.
requirements: A Claude Code login through a claude.ai account and a running Remote Control session.
Python 3.10 or newer.
Private endpoints may change; the author reports exercising list and read paths against the live API, while documenting write and control paths from client code.
MIT license.

resources.name: Spelunking
resources.description: Spelunking studies Apple apps, private frameworks and system services with Swift and Objective-C probes. It inventories runtime classes, symbols, notifications and MediaRemote state, while publishing target-specific writeups and raw captures for Messages, Phone, MediaRemote and UserNotifications.
requirements: The package requires macOS 26 or later and Swift 6.2 or later.
Individual probes may require specific OS builds, private frameworks, TCC permissions or SIP settings.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Hisense AEH-W41H1: local A/C control over a reconstructed RS-485 bus
resources.description: Hisense AEH-W41H1 local control replaces the air conditioner's cloud-connected Wi-Fi module with ESPHome firmware for an ESP32 board or the stock RTL8710C module. The implementation speaks the A/C's RS-485 bus and exposes climate controls and diagnostics to Home Assistant. Protocol notes describe the frame envelope, checksum, bus roles, and command/status behavior derived from device observation.
requirements: A Hisense A/C with an AEH-W41H1 module; the ESP32 route requires a 3.3 V RS-485 transceiver.
ESPHome 2026.10.1 for the documented ESP32 build path.
The stock-module path has no rollback without a pre-flash whole-chip dump and a SOIC-8 recovery clip; other ESPHome chips have only compile checks.
MIT License.

resources.name: whatsapp-docs
resources.description: whatsapp-docs records findings from static decompilation of the WhatsApp Android APK, covering app internals and communication formats. Its reports describe linked-device pairing, Noise transport, reporting stanzas, media upload and other client flows, with findings distinguished from inferences.
requirements: The reports use WhatsApp Android APK version 2.26.41.6 for the listed topics.
The analysis is static; server-side ML behavior is inferred from client-collected metrics.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: Hermes
resources.description: Hermes is a Flipper Zero app for identifying unknown UART settings and inspecting a device's serial console. It timestamps line edges to estimate bit time, checks candidate rates and parity against received UART bytes, then offers a terminal with text, hex and capture features. The source states that detection leaves the transmit pin undriven until the user sends data.
requirements: Flipper Zero and access to the target device's UART line.
The source says edge timing cannot follow edges beyond roughly 230400 baud; the UART sweep needs traffic during its sampling window.
MIT license.

resources.name: wMatcher
resources.description: wMatcher compares two Java archives to match classes renamed or obfuscated between releases. Its desktop workflow loads old and new JARs, accepts dependency JARs, lets the analyst correct uncertain matches and saves the comparison as a .wmatch project.
requirements: Old and new JAR files are required; dependency JARs may be added.
Building from source uses Gradle and a Java 21 toolchain.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: YGO-PoC Toolset
resources.description: YGO-PoC Toolset handles resource and save formats from Yu-Gi-Oh! Power of Chaos – Joey the Passion. Its unpacker extracts compressed game resource files such as data.dat, while PoCTools decrypts, edits and re-encrypts system.dat saves; the repository also includes a card editor and DLL mod loader.
requirements: The toolset targets the game's No-CD/Fixed executable version.
Its editor is a .NET MAUI client for PoCTools.
MIT license.

resources.name: website-to-cli
resources.description: website-to-cli is an agent skill for deriving terminal clients from captured website traffic. Its scripts record a HAR and filter requests to identify endpoint methods, paths, parameters, payload shapes and authentication headers. The skill then uses a Bun CLI template to build a client. The repository includes clients for crates.io and Hacker News search.
requirements: Bun is required for the scripts and CLI template.
Playwright is required for browser capture, or a HAR with response content can be exported from browser DevTools.
MIT license.

resources.name: FH6 Model Tools
resources.description: FH6 Model Tools parses reverse-engineered Forza Horizon 6 asset formats, including burG model and texture containers. Python converters export car meshes to GLB or OBJ, textures to DDS, and selected material, palette, lighting, and ambient-occlusion data to readable outputs.
requirements: Python 3.8 or newer and user-supplied game assets are required.
The research-status document leaves animation formats, carbin, physics data, and some material and UV semantics unresolved.
PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0.

resources.name: Cosmo: a native port of Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure
resources.description: Cosmo ports the reconstructed source of Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure: Forbidden Planet to macOS, Linux and Windows. It retains the game's logic and supplies an emulated EGA adapter, timer, keyboard controller, PC speaker and AdLib layer for the original code. The build uses the user's game data files.
requirements: A source build requires CMake 3.21+ and C11 and C++17 compilers. SDL3 can be installed or fetched by CMake; the documented Windows builds use MinGW.
A source build requires the original game data files; Episodes 2 and 3 require the user's own copies.
Joystick support is unimplemented, and frame-by-frame comparison against DOSBox remains incomplete.
MIT License.

resources.name: tuya-mobile: a Python reconstruction of Tuya app signing and API calls
resources.description: tuya-mobile reconstructs Tuya mobile-app request signing, encrypted API calls and MQTT signaling credential derivation in Python. It replaces the app's native libthing_security.so signing step with HMAC-SHA256, SHA256 and MD5 calculations and includes versioned Smart Life and Tuya Smart profiles.
requirements: Python 3.9 or newer with aiohttp and cryptography is required.
Authenticated calls require application signing constants and account authentication; password login uses a selected application profile and account credentials.
Interactive captcha, MFA, QR and social logins raise typed exceptions instead of completing login.
MIT license.

resources.name: Ed1th's PvZ Toolkit
resources.description: Ed1th's PvZ Toolkit inspects and edits Plants vs. Zombies resource archives and files through a desktop or web interface backed by Rust format libraries. Its workspaces cover RSB/RSG, PAK and DZip archives, RTON and NEWTON data, PAM animation, Compiled Text and Wwise WEM audio, among other formats.
requirements: Provide Plants vs. Zombies resource files for inspection or editing.
PAM editing does not implement curve-based tween authoring or new artwork drawing.
The BNK SoundBank browser is experimental.
AGPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: MSI Mystic Light on Linux: reconstructing B860/X870 lighting control
resources.description: MSI Mystic Light on Linux implements lighting control for an MSI motherboard from USB traffic captured while MSI Center ran in a Windows VM. Its Python script sends a 290-byte HID Feature report to controller 0db0:0076, while the documentation maps modes, RGB palette bytes, brightness, direction and the flash-save flag.
requirements: Linux, Python 3 and write access to the controller's /dev/hidraw* node.
Reverse engineered on an MSI MAG B860 TOMAHAWK WIFI; support for other boards with USB ID 0db0:0076 is stated as an expectation.
MIT license.

resources.name: LinkCam: controlling Insta360 Link 2 through UVC extension research
resources.description: LinkCam implements macOS menu-bar and command-line controls for the Insta360 Link 2 webcam. It uses standard UVC controls for pan, tilt and zoom, while its extension-unit investigation identifies a feature-mask bit and selector for AI tracking.
requirements: macOS and an Insta360 Link 2 webcam.
macOS Command Line Tools to build from source.
MIT license.

resources.name: shark-k86-mac: a client for the Attack Shark K86 HID protocol
resources.description: shark-k86-mac reconstructs the Attack Shark K86 keyboard's vendor HID controls as a Python CLI and library for macOS and Linux. Its clean-room protocol notes describe 64-byte feature reports, checksums and opcodes; the client controls lighting and the TFT screen and reads device information.
requirements: An Attack Shark K86 connected by USB in Win + USB mode is required; other models are untested.
Python 3.8+, hidapi and Pillow are required.
MIT License.

resources.name: PCM Explorer
resources.description: PCM Explorer is a read-only Python browser for Porsche PCM and Audi MMI head-unit images. It parses QNX4/QNX6 drives, compressed firmware, update discs, persistence flash and HBM5 HMI files, and supports search, image comparison, extraction and filesystem checks.
requirements: Supply an image or extracted files from a supported Porsche PCM or Audi MMI head unit.
HMI screen export produces labelled boxes rather than the original pixels.
MIT license.

resources.name: tasm-rs
resources.description: tasm-rs implements TVM bytecode assembly and disassembly in Rust, with a tdisasm CLI, instruction tables, Fift parsing and trace and coverage reports. It uses checked-in conformance fixtures to compare output with the upstream TypeScript implementation; the author reports 959 matching fixtures.
requirements: Rust 1.85 or newer for the workspace build.
The author reports byte-identical results on 959 conformance fixtures.
Deeply nested continuations have a documented compilation-time growth problem.
MIT license.

resources.name: fitdays: reconstructing a smart-scale cloud client
resources.description: fitdays recreates read-only access to the Fitdays smart-scale cloud API from traffic observed in the vendor app. Its asynchronous Python client logs in with the service's password digest, follows regional redirects, renews sessions, and retrieves scale, profile, and body-composition measurement records.
requirements: A Fitdays account is needed to retrieve its measurement history.
The client is read-only; the private endpoints may change or disappear.
MIT License.

resources.name: trvision: implementing Thermalright Vision USB display control
resources.description: trvision implements direct USB control of Thermalright Vision display panels using previously documented protocol research. It captures desktop frames, encodes JPEG or RGB565 according to the handshake reply, and sends framed data over bulk USB; a companion parser reads USBPcap captures.
requirements: Windows and Python 3.12 are specified; supported hardware is the 87AD:70DB panel family.
Close TRCC before use because it holds the USB device open.
Only 87AD:70DB panels were tested; other revisions may differ.
MIT license.

resources.name: Sogen Dart bindings
resources.description: Sogen Dart bindings expose Windows and Linux binary emulation through a Dart FFI package and native bridge. The API covers execution, snapshots, memory and registers, process views, callbacks and low-level hooks; Windows API calls and Linux symbols can also be intercepted. Its example hooks a Sleep call in an emulated executable.
requirements: Dart 3.12 or newer and Git are required.
Building requires the Visual Studio C++ desktop workload on Windows, a C++20 compiler and development headers on Linux, or Xcode command-line tools on macOS.
The example requires a Sogen emulation root.
GPL-2.0-only license.

resources.name: pocket-client: a BLE client for the Pocket voice recorder
resources.description: pocket-client implements the Pocket voice recorder's recovered BLE command protocol in a Swift library and CLI. It documents authentication, status and recording inventory exchanges, MP3 transfer and control commands, using findings from vendor-app HCI captures and live device probes.
