requirements: Requires a Pocket recorder and a session key for authenticated commands.
Requires Swift 6.0 and iOS 17 or macOS 14 or newer.
Protocol findings are based on one physical device and firmware version.
Apache-2.0 license.

resources.name: RoflLens
resources.description: RoflLens is a Python library and CLI for analysing League of Legends ROFL v2 replay containers and network transport. It exports blocks and payloads, and offers patch-specific decoders for events such as movement, spells and deaths when the client version, protocol digest and executable hash match.
requirements: Python 3.11–3.13 and a .rofl replay file are required.
Patch-specific semantic decoding requires optional dependencies and the user's exact matching League of Legends.exe.
Several gameplay semantics remain unresolved; mismatched clients receive transport-only output or an error.
MIT.

resources.name: ddg-tenor-bridge: replacing Gboard's Tenor search endpoint
resources.description: ddg-tenor-bridge redirects Gboard's Tenor GIF searches to a service that returns DuckDuckGo animated-image results in Tenor v2 response form. Its documented workflow changes Gboard's persisted search URL flag while leaving other Tenor features on their original endpoint.
requirements: A rooted Android device and an HTTPS endpoint with a publicly trusted certificate are required.
The author calls this a proof of concept; DuckDuckGo's endpoint and Gboard's version-specific flags may change.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: KeyAxis: decoding a magnetic keyboard's analog HID stream
resources.description: KeyAxis documents the HID travel stream of keyboards using the 0416:7372 controller and turns key depth into virtual gamepad axes. Its protocol notes specify the vendor interface, ARM and DISARM commands, 64-byte host reports and row, column and depth fields recovered from captured traffic.
requirements: A keyboard exposing USB ID 0416:7372 and Windows 10/11 x64 are required; gamepad output needs ViGEmBus.
Running from source requires Python 3.9 or later.
The on-screen layout covers 68 keys; vJoy output is planned.
MIT license.

resources.name: kenshi-modkit
resources.description: kenshi-modkit parses and writes Kenshi .mod and .base files and reads its .save, .zone and .platoon files using Python. Its format notes document filetypes 15–17 and inferred typecodes, while utilities dump records, compare saves, detect mod conflicts and check byte-identical round trips.
requirements: Python 3.12; standard library only.
Kenshi files are required for parsing and round-trip checks.
The author reports byte-identical round trips for 52,445 files; some typecodes remain unidentified and writing over saves is deliberately avoided.
MIT license.

resources.name: A.O. Smith water heater: local CTA-2045 control and protocol findings
resources.description: The A.O. Smith water-heater project implements local monitoring and demand-response control of an HPS10-50H45DV over its CTA-2045 RS-485 port, publishing readings to MQTT. Its documentation records frame structure, checksums, control responses and observed behavior of this specific tank.
requirements: Requires an A.O. Smith HPS10-50H45DV, a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W and an isolated RS-485 adapter as documented.
The documented setup uses Raspberry Pi OS Lite, Python 3.13 and a 19200 8N1 serial port.
Setpoint writes, water-temperature reads and operating-mode changes are unavailable through this tank's CTA-2045 port.
MIT license.

resources.name: j2208-band-tools: a direct client for the J2208 fitness-band protocol
resources.description: j2208-band-tools implements a direct BLE client for J2208-family fitness bands using protocol findings recovered from the FitTrack Health companion app. Its Python tools read stored health history and live sensor values, probe GATT services and collect readings into SQLite. The author checked the documented 16-byte frame protocol against one Hume Band V2.
requirements: A J2208-family band and Python with bleak; the companion app must release its BLE connection before the tools connect.
The author tested one Hume Band V2 with firmware v0.0.3.9; support for other family members is inferred.
Raw PPG is reported unavailable on the tested V2 firmware.
MIT license.

resources.name: Eufy Local Light: reconstructing BLE control for E10 and E22 lights
resources.description: Eufy Local Light implements a Home Assistant client for Eufy Outdoor String Lights E10 and Permanent Outdoor Lights E22 using BLE traffic analyzed from the Eufy app. Its protocol notes describe GATT endpoints, packet framing, AES-128-CBC session setup, and light-control commands.
requirements: Home Assistant and a supported Eufy light are required; development and testing covered E10 T8L10 and E22 T8L02.
The integration does not yet expose per-segment DIY patterns on the E22; E10 state readback is untested.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: OpenPeats: reconstructing SoundPEATS earbud controls
resources.description: OpenPeats reconstructs the SoundPEATS earbud control protocol for desktop and Android clients. Its specification describes frames and opcodes derived from analysis of the official Android app and checked against SOUNDPEATS H3 hardware. Go and Kotlin implementations expose ANC, equalizer and multipoint controls, plus battery status.
requirements: A paired SoundPEATS device is required; development and validation used an H3 with firmware S5_20250605_V0.4.9.
The author reports read and write validation on Linux, Windows 11, and Android.
Writing the touch mapping and touch demo mode remain unvalidated; macOS transport is unfinished and iOS SPP is unavailable.
MIT license.

resources.name: hongtai-panel: reconstructing a cooler LCD's USB serial protocol
resources.description: hongtai-panel implements Linux control of a LovingCool AIO cooler LCD using a USB CDC-ACM serial protocol reconstructed from the vendor's Electron application. Its documentation describes control-frame layout, checksums, JSON replies, and opcodes; the client displays system statistics, media, or screen mirroring.
requirements: Linux, Python 3.10+, and a supported USB LCD panel; media and mirroring features need the listed optional packages.
Other panel models are expected to work through device-reported geometry but are not identified as confirmed.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: ESPHome ↔ L&S Emotion Control: reconstructing a smart-light radio client
resources.description: An ESPHome component recreates L&S Emotion Control remote commands so an ESP32 with a CC2500 radio can control furniture lights and reflect physical remote presses in Home Assistant. Its documented radio configuration uses MSK at 2436.2 MHz, a sync word, and 14-byte payloads carrying the remote ID, command, and value.
requirements: ESP32, a 2.4 GHz CC2500 module with a 26.000 MHz crystal, soldered wiring, and an L&S Emotion Control lamp or remote.
Lamp state is estimated because the lamp provides no feedback; brightness has five levels.
Apache License 2.0.

resources.name: akp02: reconstructing the Ajazz AKP02 display protocol
resources.description: akp02 reconstructs the Ajazz AKP02 secondary display's USB HID protocol as a Linux Python library. It documents command report framing and implements full or partial image updates, brightness and power controls, firmware queries, orientation and keepalive.
requirements: An Ajazz AKP02 display and Linux HID access are required; the README describes installing a udev rule.
The package specifies Python 3.11 or newer.
MPL-2.0 license.

resources.name: cupertino-files
resources.description: cupertino-files is a TypeScript library for reading and writing modern Apple Pages, Numbers, and Keynote documents. It models their undocumented file structures from real documents, exposes editing APIs and CLI tools, and publishes format notes and a language-neutral conformance suite.
requirements: Node.js 22 or later or a modern browser; the package is ESM-only.
Modern Pages, Numbers, or Keynote documents for reading and editing.
iWork ’09 XML and password-protected documents are declined.
MIT License.

resources.name: Left 4 Dead 2: recovering the AI Director's behavior
resources.description: This Left 4 Dead 2 study reconstructs the AI Director's pacing, intensity, encounter placement and music rules from an identified x86 server.dll and sanitized runtime traces. It publishes disassembly-derived findings, analysis scripts, evidence files and implementation specifications; a reference game library is in a separate repository.
requirements: Reproducing the analysis requires an installed copy of Left 4 Dead 2, Python 3 and Capstone for disassembly scripts.
Matching RVAs require the specified June 30, 2026 x86 server.dll build.
The retail binary is stripped, leaving some private names and engine-specific helper behavior unresolved.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: MSP CSV Export Format: reconstructing My Stocks Portfolio exports
resources.description: MSP CSV Export Format reconstructs the undocumented CSV export of the My Stocks Portfolio & Market app. The author compared eleven iOS exports, app displays and public translation strings to describe columns, blocks and transaction replay. A dependency-free Python parser and synthetic export exercise the documented rules and flag malformed input.
requirements: An MSP CSV export is required for parsing personal data; Python 3.9+ is the documented runtime.
The evidence base is eleven exports from one portfolio; some locale and transaction-order behavior remains unconfirmed.
Apache-2.0 License.

resources.name: MechRewired: rebuilding MechWarrior 2 from original game data
resources.description: MechRewired rebuilds the MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat experience around data imported from a user's DOS copy. Its code loads original resources and missions, while providing a new cockpit, terrain rendering and combat simulation for modern platforms.
requirements: Requires the user's own MechWarrior 2 DOS game data; the author identifies PC English MS-DOS v1.1 as the checked package.
MIT License for the project source.

resources.name: nRF52 e-paper tag: reconstructing an undocumented display interface
resources.description: nRF52 e-paper tag reconstructs control of an undocumented electronic shelf label with an nRF52832 board and SSD1675A-class panel. The repository records the pinout, 9-bit SPI connection, waveform-table layout and refresh behavior, and provides replacement Zephyr firmware plus a portable C99 display driver.
requirements: The documented hardware uses an nRF52832, HINK-E029A10-A3 panel and ESL.CB-LR.010-00C.203 board.
The first installation requires SWD programming; building requires nRF Connect SDK v3.0.1.
MIT license.

resources.name: Benro Polaris Firmware Patcher: rebuilding camera control and mapping the app protocol
resources.description: Benro Polaris Firmware Patcher investigates the Polaris camera controller and repacks a user-supplied firmware image with a newer libgphoto2 stack and targeted pgphoto changes. Its documentation maps Benro Connect app behavior and the TCP messages used to control the device. The author reports end-to-end testing with a Canon EOS R5 Mark II.
requirements: A user-supplied stock FwPkt is required; the author tested firmware 4.0.0.32 with a Canon EOS R5 Mark II.
Optional astronomy features are experimental and have not been tested under real stars.
MIT license.

resources.name: RK M75: reconstructing wired and wireless RGB control
resources.description: RK M75 reconstructs RGB control for the Royal Kludge RK M75 keyboard from wired USB HID captures and 2.4 GHz wireless experiments. A Python library sends per-key wired frames and grouped wireless frames; the repository also contains protocol notes, captures and a wired SignalRGB plugin.
requirements: The documented hardware is an RK M75 with wired VID:PID 258A:0163 or wireless 258A:0148; development and hardware checks used Windows.
Python 3.10+ is required by the package.
The wireless protocol is partial: arbitrary per-key colors and smooth 30 FPS streaming were not achieved.
MIT license.

resources.name: d2mac-linux: porting the Diablo II Mac executable to 32-bit Linux
resources.description: d2mac-linux ports the Diablo II 1.14d Mac executable to 32-bit Linux by converting its i386 Mach-O container to ELF and reimplementing imported Darwin, Carbon and AGL interfaces in Zig. The shim translates graphics to GLX and adapts threading, files and sockets. The author reports that the game reaches its menu and character creation.
requirements: A legitimate copy of the original Diablo II Mac client and its game data is required.
Execution needs a 32-bit-capable Linux userland, Mesa GL and an X server.
Right-click handling and sound remain unimplemented.
MIT.

resources.name: PackerScope
resources.description: PackerScope scans Windows PE executables for packer signatures and structural indicators, including entropy, sections, imports and entry-point instructions. It can invoke supported unpackers and check PE integrity, entropy and import-table recovery before generating reports.
requirements: Python 3.10–3.13 is listed as the supported range.
Capstone, yara-python and ppdeep are optional analysis dependencies.
UPX unpacking requires an external upx executable.
MIT licence.

resources.name: ACiQ K18W: reconstructing a mini split's UART protocol
resources.description: ACiQ K18W documents the UART protocol between a mini split's indoor board and TCL WBR1 Wi-Fi module. Captures and decoders map 115200 8N1 traffic, 0xA5 frames, CRC-16/XMODEM, acknowledgments, and appliance fields; ESPHome configurations provide passive monitoring or local control after replacing the module.
requirements: An ACiQ ACIQ-K18W-W-32-HP2300 unit and ESP32 hardware for the documented ESPHome configurations.
Listen-only and module-replacement control are separate electrical configurations; transmit must not be enabled while the original module remains connected.
MIT license.

resources.name: RND Companion: reconstructing the RND Synth SysEx protocol
resources.description: RND Companion reconstructs the Cymaforma RND Synth's SysEx control vocabulary and implements a C++ codec and companion plugin for patch seeds. The protocol notes identify framing and seed or status commands from a web app and one hardware capture. The client can use a direct MIDI port or host MIDI routing and stores a curated seed library.
requirements: A Cymaforma RND Synth is needed for hardware use and capture.
Building the full companion requires JUCE and the separate music-suite UI source; codec tests do not require JUCE.
The wire vocabulary is based on one hardware capture and may change with firmware updates.
Unlicense public-domain dedication.

resources.name: imprint
resources.description: imprint analyzes Windows PE files by parsing import, delay-import and export directories without executing the image. It maps imported Windows APIs to categories and MITRE ATT&CK techniques, then reports capability patterns with the imports that triggered each finding in text or JSON.
requirements: A C11 compiler such as gcc, clang or MinGW is required to build it.
Imports indicate possible capabilities, not observed execution; dynamically resolved APIs and packed payloads may be hidden.
MIT license.

resources.name: Spider-Man 2 PS2 Recomp: a static recompilation checkpoint
resources.description: Spider-Man 2 PS2 Recomp applies static recompilation to the USA PlayStation 2 release SLUS-20776 for native PC execution. It combines a game-specific Ghidra function map with PS2Recomp source, runtime fixes and hardware comparison tests. The author reports that a native Windows build reaches the legal splash; the port is not playable.
requirements: A personally obtained USA Spider-Man 2 PS2 disc image and local extraction are required.
The documented Windows workflow requires Ghidra with a PS2 Emotion Engine extension, CMake and Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools.
The port is not playable; legal-splash rendering remains incomplete.
GPL-3.0 License.

resources.name: ffxii-tza-tools
resources.description: ffxii-tza-tools documents and processes FINAL FANTASY XII The Zodiac Age character formats, including .ca animations, .cm models and .phyre assets. Its Python tools decode chunk structures, export models and animations to glTF, edit curves and repack @FRP containers from files extracted from the user’s game copy.
requirements: Python 3.9 or newer and game files extracted from the user’s copy of FFXII_TZA.vbf; Pillow is needed for PNG output.
The author reports checking the documented .ca and .cm formats across the matching game files.
Blender round-trip editing and embedded .efx effect images are outside the current scope.
MIT licence.

resources.name: sims-package2glb
resources.description: sims-package2glb extracts models from The Sims 2, 3 and 4 .package files into glTF binary files. Its Rust parsers handle DBPF containers, RefPack compression, RCOL and GMDC geometry, textures, materials and recolours. The documentation records format findings including Sims 4 DST texture planes and relative RCOL chunk references.
requirements: Windows is the supported platform.
The input must be a Sims 2, 3 or 4 .package file; building from source requires Rust and Node.
MIT.

resources.name: reverse-workbench-skill
resources.description: reverse-workbench-skill is a multi-agent-harness skill bundle that routes investigations to workflows for APKs, native binaries, firmware, frontend JavaScript, and network traffic. Its documented paths include Ghidra headless exports, binary diffing, and evidence recording, alongside broader security-analysis skills and helper scripts.
requirements: A supported agent client is required; the README lists pi, Codex CLI, DSH, and Claude Code.
JDK, Node.js 22.12+, and Python 3.x are listed as prerequisites for the corresponding toolchains.
MIT license; the LICENSE retains attribution for the original reverse-skill methodology.

resources.name: vc64_240p
resources.description: vc64_240p analyses and patches the N64 Virtual Console emulator inside Wii WAD channels to output 240p. It finds render-mode structures by pattern, changes video fields and disables deflicker; an optional patch removes the emulator's dark filter.
requirements: A user-supplied N64 Virtual Console WAD and a separately generated Wii common key are required.
Installing output on Wii requires cIOS 249 and Priiloader or BootMii.
PAL is unsupported, and the author reports live checks on five emulator builds.
MIT.

resources.name: RtG-Format
resources.description: RtG-Format documents the observed save and construction format of the Roblox game Road To Gramby's. Its references and experiments cover build structures, part identifiers, connections, properties, encoding and compression, with supporting CLI and browser preview tools.
requirements: The project states that reverse engineering is ongoing and some field meanings and behavior remain uncertain.
GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: Malware Analysis: a trojanized FL Studio installer and Go stealer
resources.description: This malware-analysis report investigates a trojanized FL Studio installer that bundles an Electron/NSIS wrapper and a Go information stealer. The author traces the wrapper statically and studies the payload in an isolated Windows environment with process, registry and network observations, recovering its reported command-and-control mechanism.
requirements: The author used an isolated KVM/QEMU Windows guest and a simulated network for dynamic observations.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: MindNode MCP Server
resources.description: MindNode MCP Server connects agents to MindNode Next mind maps on macOS. Its reader decodes the app's SQLite library, protobuf snapshots, Apple LZ4 compression and CRDT operations into Markdown outlines; other MCP tools return previews or create maps through MindNode's Markdown importer.
requirements: macOS with MindNode 2024+ and Node.js 24 or later.
The author checked the format on MindNode 2026.4.4; heavily edited text may decode incorrectly.
MIT license.

resources.name: touhou-engine: a Python reimplementation of Touhou gameplay
resources.description: touhou-engine reimplements Touhou danmaku gameplay in Python, with TH07: Perfect Cherry Blossom as its reference game. The author says its engine logic was ported frame by frame against a decompilation, while the new architecture supplies an event stream, replay handling, headless stepping, and a pygame renderer. It reads original game archives supplied by the user.
requirements: Requires Python 3.12 or newer and the documented numpy, pillow, pygame, loguru, and msgspec dependencies.
Requires the user's own TH07 data archive; BGM uses thbgm.dat from the same directory.
The source attributes its decompilation reference to some100/th07.

resources.name: viture-v2: a reconstructed VITURE Gen2 glasses protocol and driver
resources.description: viture-v2 documents and implements the USB HID protocol used by VITURE Gen2 XR glasses. The author matched usbmon captures to SDK frame logs, then wrote a Rust driver with hidraw, usbfs and io_uring transports for queries and IMU streams. Measurements and compatibility claims cover the VITURE Pro 2 XR.
requirements: A VITURE Gen2 XR device and a supported Linux or Android USB transport are required for hardware use.
Only VITURE Pro 2 XR was measured; setters remain unmapped.
MIT License.

resources.name: BikeStation: local Echelon Connect control over Bluetooth LE
resources.description: BikeStation is a local Windows client for Echelon Connect exercise bikes built on community research into their proprietary Bluetooth LE protocol. It reads cadence and resistance telemetry, queries the bike's resistance range, writes motorized resistance commands and records rides without the vendor cloud.
requirements: A Windows PC with Bluetooth and an Echelon bike advertising a name beginning with ECH are required.
The author reports end-to-end testing on a Connect EX-5 only; resistance writing requires a motorized resistance mechanism.
GPL-3.0-or-later.

resources.name: grsimwrite-mac: reconstructing GRSIMWrite for macOS
resources.description: grsimwrite-mac reconstructs the Windows GRSIMWrite 4.4.10 SIM-writing workflow in Python for macOS. Its research records card-family profiles and APDU write behavior, while the implementation identifies cards, reads elementary files, writes selected fields, and builds formatting sequences.
requirements: macOS, a PC/SC card reader, and the pyscard and pydes dependencies are required for card operation.
The author reports 41 offline unit tests using mocks, without hardware.
No licence file in the repository.

resources.name: kdemulator
resources.description: kdemulator executes Windows x86-64 kernel-driver binaries outside a live kernel for IOCTL analysis. It maps PE sections into Unicorn, intercepts imported NT API calls and supplies minimal kernel-object and memory stubs. The CLI can invoke DriverEntry, send one IOCTL or run a mutation loop over an IOCTL input buffer.
requirements: Windows x86-64 driver .sys files are the documented inputs.
Emulation covers only the driver's own code and directly imported functions; hardware-facing drivers need additional stubs.
Unlicense.

resources.name: angr-management
resources.description: Cross-platform graphical binary analysis tool powered by the angr platform, with disassembly and decompilation views.
requirements: Powered by the angr platform; v10.0.5 is dated 2026-10-22.
BSD-2-Clause per LICENSE.

resources.name: QIRA
resources.description: QIRA is a tool for examining program execution traces. Its interface lets users navigate instruction changes, register values, memory reads and writes, and forks.
requirements: Ubuntu 14.04 and 16.04 are supported out of the box.
The QEMU tracer requires a Linux host; native Mac OS X and Windows support is very limited.
QIRA code is licensed under MIT; other code in the repository retains its respective licenses.

resources.name: Dependencies
resources.description: Dependencies is a Windows PE dependency analysis tool with command-line and graphical interfaces. It shows imports, exports, and DLL load dependencies to help diagnose loading problems.
requirements: Requires the Visual C++ Redistributable to run properly.
Does not detect dependencies loaded dynamically through LoadLibrary.
Recursive analysis must be enabled in the options and can use substantial memory.
The repository declares the MIT license.

resources.name: dnlib
resources.description: dnlib is a .NET library for reading and writing modules and assemblies. It provides access to metadata, method bodies, resources, and PDB files.
requirements: For .NET Core assemblies, disable GAC loading and add .NET Core reference assembly search paths.
Writing Windows PDB files requires Windows.
Licensed under MIT.

resources.name: Hachoir
resources.description: Hachoir is a Python library for viewing and editing binary streams as trees of fields, down to individual bits. Its command-line tools can search binary files for text, extract or remove metadata, and display file contents in text mode.
requirements: Requires Python 3.7 or newer.
Licensed under GNU GPL v2.

resources.name: Pigaios
resources.description: Pigaios is a tool that matches C source code against binaries in IDA. It extracts function features from source code, finds corresponding functions in an IDA database, and imports symbols, structures, and enumerations. It can work with partial source code that does not compile.
requirements: Requires Python Clang bindings; the README indicates Clang 3.9 or later should work.
Requires IDA with IDAPython to match binaries and import the results.
On Windows, LLVM must be installed and added to PATH. Colorama is optional for colors, and scikit-learn is optional for machine learning features.
License: GPL-3.0.

resources.name: MachOExplorer
resources.description: MachOExplorer is a desktop and command-line tool for inspecting Mach-O binaries, Universal binaries, static archives, and dyld shared caches. It displays file structures, symbols, disassembly, and Apple-specific metadata, and can export analysis as text or JSON.
requirements: Building from source requires CMake 3.16 or later, Qt 6, and a C++14 compiler.
Capstone is optional and enables disassembly.
Prebuilt releases are available for macOS; Linux and Windows require source builds.
The repository declares the MIT license.

resources.name: me_cleaner
resources.description: me_cleaner is a Python script that modifies Intel ME firmware images to reduce the firmware's ability to interact with the system. Depending on the ME generation, it removes the firmware or retains only modules needed for boot.
requirements: Requires Python and an original Intel ME firmware image.
Flashing the modified image often requires an external SPI programmer.
Board support varies; some OEM firmware will not boot after modification, and Intel ME features will no longer work.
License: GPL-3.0.

resources.name: FLEX
resources.description: FLEX is an in-app tool for exploring and debugging running iOS applications. It can inspect and change views and object state, browse app files and databases, and show network request history.
requirements: Needs an app that targets iOS 9 or higher, and FLEX should be excluded from release builds.
BSD-style terms per LICENSE.

resources.name: classdump-dyld
resources.description: classdump-dyld is a command-line tool that generates Objective-C headers from Mach-O app binaries, libraries, frameworks, bundles, and images in the dyld shared cache. It can dump a single class or process compatible files recursively.
requirements: Requires a command-line shell on an iOS 5+ device or Mac OS X.
Works with Mach-O files only.
Some files cannot be dumped when protection prevents dynamic loading from another process.
GPL-3.0 per the README.

resources.name: View8
resources.description: View8 is a static analysis tool that decompiles serialized V8 bytecode (JSC) files into readable JavaScript-like text. It can also export opcodes, parsed objects, and function trees organized by declarations, calls, or references.
requirements: Python 3.x is required.
Raw JSC input requires a compatible patched V8 disassembler binary; the listed versions are 9.4.146.24, 10.2.154.26, and 11.3.244.8.
Serialized input uses Python pickle and must come from a trusted source.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: unwebpack-sourcemap
resources.description: unwebpack-sourcemap is a Python script that recovers TypeScript, JSX, and other source files from Webpack source maps. It accepts local or remote source maps and can search a web page's scripts for them.
requirements: Requires Python 3, BeautifulSoup4, and requests.
Intended for TypeScript with React or Vue templates.
The repository is archived and is not being maintained.
Licensed under MIT.

resources.name: Wirebrowser
resources.description: Wirebrowser is a desktop tool for instrumenting browser JavaScript through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It can hook functions, trace where values originate, search and modify runtime objects, and intercept or replay HTTP traffic.
requirements: Use a macOS, Windows, or Linux desktop build, or build from source with npm.
On Linux with the AppImage, keep the installed Chrome extension in its visible directory under the home directory.
The repository declares the MIT License.

resources.name: Process Dump
resources.description: Process Dump is a Windows command-line tool that saves code from running processes to disk for malware analysis. It can find hidden modules and loose executable code, reconstruct PE headers and imports, and use a clean-hash database to skip known modules.
requirements: Runs on 32-bit and 64-bit Windows through the matching standalone executable; run as Administrator for best access. Release v3.0.0 is dated 2026-10-03.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: mal_unpack
resources.description: mal_unpack is a Windows dynamic unpacker based on PE-sieve. It runs a packed malware executable, waits for its payload to unpack, dumps the payload, and terminates the original process.
requirements: Run on Windows and provide a packed malware executable.
Use only in a virtual machine because the tool launches the original malware.
License: BSD-2-Clause.

resources.name: Unrpyc
resources.description: Unrpyc is a tool that decompiles compiled Ren'Py game scripts into readable script files. It runs from the command line or through files placed in a game's directory; it does not extract RPA archives.
requirements: Use Python 3.9 or later for Unrpyc v2, or Python 2.7 for v1.
Choose the version for the game's Ren'Py release; v2 game injection supports Ren'Py 8, while v1 supports Ren'Py 6 and 7.
MIT per the README and LICENSE.

resources.name: BSPSource
resources.description: Java map decompiler that turns Source engine .bsp map files back into .vmf files that can be loaded in Hammer. It also has an integrated pakfile extractor.
requirements: The cross-platform JAR package requires Java 24 or later, installed and configured.
GoldSrc and Source 2 maps are unsupported.
Some internal entities cannot be restored perfectly.
Released into the public domain per LICENSE.md.

resources.name: OGhidra
resources.description: OGhidra is an AI integration for analyzing binaries with Ghidra through natural language. It supports function analysis, automated renaming, malware pattern detection, and either an MCP or PyGhidra backend.
requirements: Python 3.12 or later and Ghidra; version 12.0.3 is recommended.
Java 21 is required to build the Ghidra 12.0.3 extension.
Configure a local or external AI provider; the MCP backend requires a running Ghidra client, while PyGhidra requires a valid Ghidra project or a binary to import.
BSD 3-Clause with a commercial license alternative, per LICENSE.

resources.name: aiDAPal
resources.description: aiDAPal is an IDA Pro plugin that uses a locally hosted language model trained for Hex-Rays pseudocode to assist with code analysis. It presents generated changes for acceptance before updating the pseudocode.
requirements: IDA Pro with Hex-Rays is required.
Ollama must be configured with the downloaded model weights and modelfile.
The plugin requires the Python requests package; its default configuration connects to a local Ollama service.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: OpenLara: Tomb Raider engine reimplementation
resources.description: Open-source engine for classic Tomb Raider, with a WebGL build and a standalone release. Its format code defines object types for Tomb Raider 1 through 4.
requirements: The repository declares the BSD-2-Clause license.

resources.name: Thyme: Command & Conquer Generals: Zero Hour reimplementation
resources.description: Thyme is an open source reimplementation of Command & Conquer Generals: Zero Hour. It rewrites the game from the ground up and uses the original binary for functions it has not yet replaced.
requirements: Running Thyme requires an installed copy of Command & Conquer Generals: Zero Hour.
Building a working binary requires Microsoft Visual Studio 2017 or later.
Thyme currently runs only on Windows; its custom launcher supports the English disc version patched to 1.04.
The repository is archived.
License: GPL-2.0.

resources.name: Chariot: Age of Empires engine reimplementation
resources.description: Chariot is an open-source effort to reimplement the engine of the original Age of Empires (1997). It aims to support ports and enhancements; the README describes it as a work in progress with asset-loading demonstrations, not a playable game.
requirements: Building requires Rust, a supported C/C++ compiler, and SDL2.
Running requires an original Age of Empires CD for game data.
The README reports that the project was not yet playable as of 2016-07-08.
The README declares an MIT license.

resources.name: OpenDiablo2: Diablo 2 engine reimplementation
resources.description: OpenDiablo2 is a cross-platform ARPG engine written in Go that supports playing Diablo 2. The project is being split into a separate engine and toolset, called Abyss Engine, and a game project retaining the OpenDiablo2 name.
requirements: Playing Diablo 2 requires a legally purchased copy of Diablo 2 and its Lord of Destruction expansion installed on the computer.
The project does not include the assets or content needed to play Diablo 2.
The repository is archived.
License: GPL-3.0.

resources.name: Black Magic Debug
resources.description: Black Magic Debug is a self-contained debugger for microcontrollers. It detects and configures connected targets without configuration files.
requirements: Needs a connected microcontroller target.
The project moved to Codeberg, and this GitHub repository is archived.
GPL-3.0 per COPYING, with BSD and MIT license files for parts of the code.

resources.name: OpenOCD
resources.description: OpenOCD is a tool for programming and debugging embedded targets through hardware debug adapters. It supports flash programming, breakpoints, single stepping, and remote debugging through GDB.
requirements: Hardware access requires a supported adapter and a target configuration.
Source builds require GCC or Clang, make, libtool, pkg-config 0.23 or newer or pkgconf, and libjim 0.79 or newer.
GPL-2.0-or-later per COPYING.

resources.name: LogicAnalyzer
resources.description: LogicAnalyzer is a hardware and software tool for capturing digital signals and decoding communication protocols. It supports triggered capture, multiple channels, and Sigrok protocol decoders.
requirements: Requires supported Pico hardware, matching firmware, and capture software.
Licensed under GPL-3.0.

resources.name: BtleJuice
resources.description: BtleJuice is a framework for intercepting Bluetooth Low Energy GATT operations between devices. Its web interface displays intercepted operations and supports replay, data modification, and export.
requirements: Requires Node.js 4.3.2 or newer, npm, and the listed Bluetooth system dependencies.
The core and proxy require separate machines with two Bluetooth 4.0 or newer adapters.
The proxy does not work in a Docker container.
The repository is archived and has no license file.

resources.name: NearDrop
resources.description: macOS menu bar app that partially implements Nearby Share and Quick Share to exchange files and links with Android devices. Its protocol document describes the protocol as understood from Chromium sources and a decompiled Google Services Framework APK.
requirements: Requires a Mac and an Android device on the same Wi-Fi network.
Android devices must be publicly visible when connecting through NearDrop’s QR code.
Works over Wi-Fi LAN only and remains visible to everyone on the network while running.
License: Unlicense.

resources.name: x64dbg MCP Server Plugin
resources.description: An MCP server plugin for x64dbg and x32dbg that lets external applications and AI agents control debugging through HTTP. It provides tools for execution, memory, registers, breakpoints, and disassembly, along with debugger context resources and workflow prompts.
requirements: Requires a 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 host and x64dbg or x32dbg build 2023 or later.
Building requires CMake 3.15 or later, Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ Desktop Development workload, vcpkg, and Git.
Debugging operations require the debugger to be paused; memory and register writes are disabled by default.
License: MIT.

resources.name: JEB-MCP
resources.description: JEB-MCP is an MCP server and JEB Pro script that lets MCP clients inspect and rename elements of Android apps in JEB. Its documented commands include reading decompiled code, examining classes and methods, and renaming them.
requirements: JEB Pro with the project script started in its GUI.
Python 3.11 or later and uv.
An MCP client configured to connect to the server.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: re-shell
resources.description: re-shell is a Nix flake development environment that provides Claude Code with reverse engineering tools and workflows. Its skills select guidance for Windows binaries, Android packages, and web captures based on the files being analyzed.
requirements: Nix with the nix-command and flakes experimental features enabled.
Claude Code for the file-specific skills and workflows.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: ghidra-rpc
resources.description: ghidra-rpc is a CLI integration that lets AI coding assistants use a persistent Ghidra session for binary analysis. It returns structured JSON for tasks such as decompilation, symbol annotation, type recovery, patching, and binary version comparison.
requirements: Requires Ghidra 11+, Python 3.11+, Java 17+, and uv.
An AI coding assistant must be able to run shell commands to drive a session.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: Bloaty
resources.description: Bloaty is a binary size profiler that attributes file and memory usage to sources such as symbols, compilation units, and sections. It can compare sizes between binaries and supports ELF and Mach-O, with experimental PE/COFF and WebAssembly support.
requirements: CMake is required to build the project.
Check out the Git submodules when building from a clone that did not include them.
PE/COFF and WebAssembly support is experimental.
The repository declares the Apache-2.0 license.

resources.name: Soot
resources.description: Soot is a Java optimization framework for analyzing and transforming Java bytecode. It provides four intermediate representations, including forms suited to optimization, decompilation, and code inspection.
requirements: Requires a Java runtime and Java classes or bytecode to analyze.
Available as a dependency through Maven, Gradle, or SBT, or as a JAR.
The repository declares the LGPL-2.1 license.

resources.name: bingrep
resources.description: bingrep is a command-line tool for inspecting and colorizing binary files. It displays details from ELF, Mach, Unix and BSD archives, and PE files, with experimental views of hexadecimal data and file offset ranges.
requirements: Building requires rustc 1.74 or later.
PE support is debug only.
The repository declares the MIT license.

resources.name: libPeConv
resources.description: libPeConv is a Windows library for loading and manipulating PE files. It supports tasks such as section remapping, relocation, import loading, resource parsing, and rebuilding import address tables from memory dumps.
requirements: Requires Windows.
Applications that use MUI are unsupported.
License: BSD-2-Clause.

resources.name: Viper
resources.description: Viper is a framework for binary analysis and for organizing malware samples, exploit samples, and research scripts. The Viper 1.x repository is archived and development has ended.
requirements: Install with pip3.
Viper 1.x is archived and no longer developed; the refactor continues as Viper 2.
BSD-3-Clause per LICENSE.

resources.name: DroidLysis
resources.description: DroidLysis is a pre-analysis tool for Android apps that disassembles samples, organizes their contents, and flags code patterns for further inspection. It accepts APK, DEX, ODEX, ARM executable, ZIP, RAR, and directory inputs.
requirements: Requires Python 3 and the listed system packages, including a Java runtime.
Requires Apktool and Baksmali, with their locations set in the configuration file; Dex2jar is optional.
Known third-party SDKs are excluded from analysis by default unless the relevant option is enabled.
The repository declares the MIT license.

resources.name: PKHeX
resources.description: PKHeX is a C# Windows Forms editor for Pokémon core-series save data. It can edit and save supported files, import Pokémon and teams, and convert data between game generations.
requirements: Requires .NET 10.
Save files must be free of console-specific encryption; a save-data manager is needed to move saves to and from a console.
License: GPLv3.

resources.name: Thug
resources.description: Thug is a Python low-interaction honeyclient that mimics a web browser to detect and emulate malicious content. It supports the study of client-side attacks.
requirements: GPL-2.0 per the README.

resources.name: Cuckoo3
resources.description: Cuckoo3 is a malware analysis tool that tests suspicious files and links in sandboxed platform emulators. It reports what the files or websites did during the test.
requirements: Requires a Linux (Ubuntu) host with Python 3.10 and Windows sandboxes.
The README says it is not ready for production use.
License: EUPL-1.2.

resources.name: Cuckoo Sandbox
resources.description: Cuckoo Sandbox is an automated malware analysis system that executes suspicious files in an isolated environment and reports their behavior.
requirements: The README marks Cuckoo Sandbox 2.x as unmaintained and the repository is archived.
GPL-3.0 per docs/LICENSE.

resources.name: fq
resources.description: fq is a command-line tool and query language for inspecting and decoding binary formats. It provides a structural hex viewer, bit-level decoding, nested format parsing, and an interactive query interface.
requirements: Go 1.22 or later is required to build from source.
The repository declares the MIT License.

resources.name: innoextract
resources.description: Unpacks Inno Setup installers on non-Windows systems without running them. It also handles modified variants, including GOG.com's Inno Setup-based game installers.
requirements: Building requires Boost 1.37 or newer, CMake 2.8 or newer, and a working C++ compiler.
liblzma is optional, but most installers made with newer Inno Setup versions cannot be extracted without it.
Individual components cannot be selected for extraction, and filtering by name is limited.
License: ZLIB.

resources.name: Metasm
resources.description: Metasm is a Ruby suite for assembling, disassembling, debugging, and modifying executable binaries. It supports formats including PE, ELF, Mach-O, and shellcode.
requirements: Ruby is required to use the suite and its sample scripts.
LGPL per the README; the LICENCE file carries LGPL-2.1.

resources.name: OpenTomb: Tomb Raider engine reimplementation
resources.description: OpenTomb is an open-source reimplementation of the classic Tomb Raider engine for playing levels from Tomb Raider 1–5 and custom TRLE levels. It is no longer maintained.
requirements: Playing original game levels requires assets from the corresponding games.
Building from source requires C++11 and the development dependencies listed in the README.
CD audio is supported only in OGG format.
License: LGPL-3.0.

resources.name: Savage Wind Recomp: statically recompiling The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
resources.description: Savage Wind Recomp is an in-progress static recompilation of the Nintendo Switch version of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild for Windows and Linux. It builds native game code locally from the player's extracted files; the README reports playable early areas but says the full story remains unconfirmed.
requirements: Requires a personally obtained and extracted Nintendo Switch copy of the game with update 1.9.0; game files are not included.
Requires Windows 10 or later or Linux, a 64-bit CPU with SSE4.2, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU, 16 GB of RAM, and about 20 GB of free disk space.
The project is in alpha; later parts of the main story may have bugs or crashes.
MIT per LICENSE.

resources.name: retruxx: reverse-engineered Hard Truck Apocalypse
resources.description: retruxx is a reverse-engineered Hard Truck Apocalypse project that builds the game executable and separate renderer, input, and sound DLLs. Its 32-bit build matches the original game's memory layouts.
requirements: Building requires Windows, Visual Studio C++ build tools, CMake, Git, the DirectX SDK (June 2010), and the FMOD Core SDK.
Running the game requires an installed copy of Ex Machina / Hard Truck Apocalypse for its game data.
The executable and driver DLLs must have compatible bitness.
The repository has no license file.

resources.name: nxnative
resources.description: nxnative is a tool that packages Nintendo Switch games as apps that run their code natively on Apple hardware, with graphics translated to Metal. It builds iPhone, iPad, or Mac apps from supported Switch games; Switch 2 builds are documented for Mac only.
requirements: Building requires a Mac with macOS 26.6 or later, Xcode 27.2, Homebrew, and arm64 Python 3.12 or later.
Switch game builds require the user's game files and prod.keys; Switch 2 builds use a NUP file or extracted game files and do not require prod.keys.
iPhone and iPad play requires iOS or iPadOS 26 or later and the specified newer hardware; Switch 2 games are documented for Mac only.
License: MIT.

resources.name: Impacket
resources.description: Impacket is a Python library for constructing and parsing network packets and working with protocol implementations. It covers protocols including SMB and MSRPC and includes example tools.
requirements: Requires Python 3; the README recommends pipx for system-wide installation.
The README describes the software as intended for research and education, not production or commercial use.
Apache Software License with slight modifications, per LICENSE.

resources.name: r0idamcp
resources.description: r0idamcp is a single-file MCP server that connects IDA Pro to an MCP-capable assistant for automated reverse engineering. Its tools expose functions, strings, decompilation, cross-references, comments, and renaming through an SSE connection.
requirements: IDA Pro is required; version 8.3 or later is recommended.
Install FastMCP with pip into the Python environment used by IDA Pro.
Use an MCP client that can connect to an SSE server, and allow access to the configured server port.
License: MIT.

resources.name: SOMCP
resources.description: SOMCP is an Android MCP server for analyzing and modifying native SO libraries. It exposes ELF analysis, disassembly, patching, and optional dynamic analysis tools to MCP clients.
requirements: Requires Android 8.0 or later.
Emulation in official release APKs requires a 64-bit device; Frida features require a separately installed Frida server or gadget on a rooted device.
The repository declares the AGPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: VirtualXposed
resources.description: VirtualXposed is an Android app that runs Xposed modules alongside apps in a virtual environment without root access, an unlocked bootloader, or a custom system image. It is based on VirtualApp and epic.
requirements: Requires an Android 5.0–10.0 device and installation of the VirtualXposed APK.
Apps and Xposed modules must both be installed inside VirtualXposed for modules to take effect.
Modules that modify the system and resource hooks are unsupported; the README prohibits commercial use.
The repository declares the GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: EdXposed Framework
resources.description: EdXposed is a Riru module that provides an Xposed-compatible ART hooking framework for Android 8.0 through 11. It lets Xposed modules change system and app behavior without modifying APKs.
requirements: Android 8.0 through 11.
Magisk v21+ and Riru v23+.
EdXposed Manager for the documented installation process.
License: GPL-3.0.

resources.name: Vector Framework
resources.description: Vector Framework is a Zygisk module that provides ART hooking for Android apps. It supports Xposed APIs and lets modules change app and system behavior in memory without modifying APK files.
requirements: Requires Android 8.1 through Android 17 Beta.
Requires a recent Magisk or KernelSU installation with Zygisk enabled.
Licensed under GPL-3.0.

resources.name: JustTrustMe
resources.description: JustTrustMe is an Xposed module that disables SSL certificate checks in Android apps. It can help expose network traffic from apps that use certificate pinning.
requirements: Requires a rooted Android device.
Requires the Xposed framework to be installed.
Apache-2.0 per License.md.

resources.name: spy-debugger
resources.description: spy-debugger is a tool for remotely debugging pages in mobile browsers and app WebViews while capturing HTTP and HTTPS traffic. It injects weinre debugging code into HTML responses and can use its built-in proxy or an external one.
requirements: Install spy-debugger with npm on a computer.
Connect the phone and computer to the same network and configure the phone's HTTP proxy.
Install a certificate on the phone for HTTPS debugging; on iOS 15, the tool cannot identify whether a request came from a browser.
License: MIT.
